# 🔧 MACHINE · QUERY AND LOGIC
*Aspirational, not demand-driven — the opposite contract from THE MIDDLE
LAYER above. specimens: 1 (owner's own long-standing want, stated live
2026-08-28 — "you have no idea how long I've wanted both a SQL function and
a PROLOG function inside Excel" — not corpus demand, so this tranche stays
thin and appetite-boxed rather than hydrated). Buy the decision now; defer
the artifact.*

- ⬜ **`SQL(table, query)`** — a relational query engine as a real worksheet
  function, prompted by `scripts/spreadsheet.lisp`'s own `SELECTFROM`/
  `SELECTROWS` (an Excel-native `LAMBDA`+`BYROW`+`FILTER` implementation)
  crashing on large tables. **The one binding architectural decision:** it
  must be declared `function`, never `deflambda` — `deflambda` compiles to
  exactly one native Excel `LAMBDA` formula expression, so it inherits
  `BYROW`'s per-row recalculation ceiling no matter how the query is
  worded; a straight port of the Lisp version's approach would hit the
  identical wall. `function` gives a real imperative VBA UDF: one
  `Range.Value2` read into a Variant array, one native loop, one array
  write-back — the standard high-performance Excel/VBA pattern, and the
  actual fix.
  - **MVP** (`~weeks`): `SELECT`/`WHERE`/`ORDER BY`/`LIMIT` over a single
    table. WHERE is a real recursive-descent parse (AND/OR, parens,
    comparators) into a small expression tree, not `EXTRACTOPERATOR`'s
    string-`FIND` heuristics — those can't handle precedence or nesting.
    Column names resolved once via a `Dictionary`, keyed through
    `VLA_Identity.Fold` (reusing the existing fold rather than a second
    `LCase`, so this doesn't reintroduce the Turkish-`I` locale bug the
    neutrality audit already flags elsewhere in this file). Matched rows
    collected into a manually-doubled buffer, never `ReDim Preserve` per
    row (that's the O(n²) trap that would silently reintroduce the exact
    performance problem this item exists to fix).
  - **Full relational** (`~months`, staged): multi-table `JOIN` (always a
    hash join — build a `Dictionary` on the smaller side, probe with the
    larger; nested-loop join is not an acceptable implementation at any
    table size), `GROUP BY`/`HAVING`/aggregates, subqueries and `WITH`
    CTEs, `UNION`/`INTERSECT`/`EXCEPT`, window functions, computed
    `SELECT` expressions.
  - **Ceiling**: a persistent index cache keyed by (range address,
    dimensions, a cheap content checksum), surviving across recalcs so
    repeat queries against the same big table don't re-scan; `EXPLAIN`
    returning the parsed logical plan instead of executing it, matching
    this project's existing auditability-before-procedural-power stance
    rather than shipping a bigger black box.
  - **Explicit non-goal:** `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`. A worksheet function
    mutating cells outside its own return value is the exact anti-pattern
    Excel's calc engine exists to prevent — real DML would have to live as
    an imperative `sub`/macro command (the `latin.vla` style), never as
    part of this `function`.

- ⬜ **`PROLOG(knowledgebase, query)`** — the existing toy (`_1_is_2.`,
  `_Is_1_2?`, `QUESTION`/`STATEMENT` in `scripts/spreadsheet.lisp`) grown
  from sentence-string pattern matching into real unification and
  backtracking over structured facts/rules. **Free-form English-to-query
  translation is explicitly out of scope for this item** — not a technical
  deferral, the owner's own call, this session: Frazaro's whole premise is
  that one deterministic phrasing keeps translation cheap, so if a natural-
  language front end is ever wanted here it is a phrasebook problem (new
  `{slot:type}` grammar rows targeting `(fact ...)`/`(rule ...)` forms,
  F.4-checked like every other rule), never a free-parse problem, and
  shares no design risk with the engine below. **This engine's contract is
  general unification plus backtracking search — not guaranteed to
  terminate**, by design (that's what full Prolog is); the restricted,
  always-terminating fragment is `DATALOG`'s job, below, on purpose kept as
  a separate name rather than an auto-detected mode of this one — see that
  item for why.
  - **v0** (`~weeks`): facts only (`(fact (parent tom bob))`), conjunctive
    queries, no rules, no KB-side variables. Reuses VLA's own S-expression
    reader to parse `(fact ...)` forms straight out of a cell range — no
    second parser needed, the one architectural gift this item gets for
    free from already being a Lisp.
  - **v1** (`~weeks` more): `(rule head body...)` forms, unification with a
    `Dictionary`-backed substitution environment, depth-first SLD
    resolution with backtracking, no cut. All-solutions surfaced as a
    spilled array — one row per solution, one column per free query
    variable — the same shape `SELECTROWS` already uses, not a lazy stream
    (VBA has none).
  - **v1's unifier is substrate, not engine-private** (scoped 2026-08-29;
    full text in `BETA_ROADMAP.md`'s own entry): built as `VLA_Unify.bas`,
    `VLA_Relation.bas`'s sibling, with two modes from one walker — one-way
    match (ground on one side; G-RENDER's already-shipped `UnifyForm` in
    `VLA_English.bas` is exactly this case and becomes a thin client,
    keeping only its English-specific glued-slot branch as an atom-level
    hook) and two-way unify (Prolog proper, occurs check refused by name,
    `prolog-occurs-check`, never skipped for speed). Pays into G-RENDER v2
    (multi-statement templates are the unifier's list case), OPTIMIZE's
    grounding, and SD-16 — the unifier matches forms against forms and is
    never handed a token stream.
  - **v2** (`~weeks` more): cut, `is`/arithmetic, negation-as-failure,
    `findall`/aggregation.
  - **Ceiling** (`~months`): first-argument clause indexing (the Prolog
    twin of `SQL`'s hash-join law — don't scan every clause per call);
    tabling/memoized resolution (SLG), which is what actually terminates
    the textbook `ancestor(X,Y) :- ancestor(X,Z), parent(Z,Y)` recursive
    case rather than infinite-looping, and is the difference between a toy
    backtracker and something that survives a real KB; an `EXPLAIN` that
    returns the proof tree (which facts/rules fired, in order) for the
    same auditability reason as `SQL`'s. **Constraint/CSP solving is
    explicitly not this engine's job** — that instinct belongs to `OPTIMIZE`
    below (Answer Set Programming), which is a purpose-built generate-
    and-test notation for "many valid worlds, pick the best," not a
    repurposed proof engine wearing an `in`/`all_different` costume.

- ⬜ **`DATALOG(tables, rules)`** — the guaranteed-terminating third engine,
  scoped out explicitly rather than folded into either function above.
  **The grammar itself refuses any rule containing a compound term as an
  argument** (no `f(g(X))` nesting — variables and constants only),
  enforced at parse time, not detected at runtime. That restriction is the
  entire feature: it's what makes every `DATALOG()` query provably
  terminate, the same way stratified negation below is checked and refused
  at parse time rather than discovered live. **Considered and rejected:**
  letting `PROLOG()` auto-detect a function-free ruleset and silently run
  it bottom-up instead of backtracking. Rejected because that trades a
  visible contract for an invisible one — a query that loses its
  termination guarantee the moment one rule happens to use a compound
  term, with no signal to the author that anything changed, is the exact
  opposite of this project's own auditability-before-procedural-power
  instinct (169 hand-written refusal strings and F.4's conflict analyzer
  both refuse loudly and specifically rather than silently working
  around).
  - **The killer case, concretely:** facts don't require a `(fact ...)` KB
    block — they can be **an existing worksheet range, read directly**.
    An `Employees` table with a `manager_id` column *is* a
    `reports_to(employee, manager)` relation with no authoring step at
    all; two rules (`indirect_report(X,Y) :- reports_to(X,Y).` /
    `indirect_report(X,Y) :- reports_to(X,Z), indirect_report(Z,Y).`)
    compute the full org chart's transitive closure over live data. Same
    shape for bill-of-materials explosion (`part_of`), dependency
    closure — any "everything transitively under this row" question,
    which is the one query shape neither `SQL()`'s MVP (no recursion) nor
    `PROLOG()` (unification/backtracking overhead, no termination
    guarantee) answers well.
  - **MVP** (`~weeks`): function-free Horn clauses only (parse-time
    refusal of anything else), facts sourced from a range or a
    `(fact ...)` block, semi-naive bottom-up fixpoint evaluation reusing
    `SQL`'s hash-join/indexed-relation substrate directly, results as a
    spilled array — same output shape as `SQL`/`PROLOG`.
  - **Stretch** (`~weeks` more): stratified negation (`not`, safe only
    because stratifiability — no predicate negatively depending on
    itself — is checked and refused at parse time) and grouped
    aggregation (`count`/`sum` per group, the Datalog analogue of `SQL`'s
    `GROUP BY`).
  - **Sequencing note:** the smallest of the three engines — no
    compound-term unification, no backtracking, no cut — and it exercises
    the shared indexed-relation substrate directly. Worth building
    **before** `SQL`'s full-relational tier or `PROLOG`'s ceiling tier: it
    proves the shared-substrate bet cheaply instead of discovering its
    problems mid-way through a bigger engine.

- ⬜ **`OPTIMIZE(facts, program)`** — Answer Set Programming, the fourth and
  last of this family, complementary rather than competing: the other
  three all answer some version of "what follows from what I know"; this
  one answers "what are all the self-consistent ways this could be, and
  which is best." Written like `DATALOG` (facts, rules) plus two new
  ingredients — **choice rules** (`{ assign(S,P) : eligible(P,S) } = 2 :-
  shift(S).`, "generate every possible way to pick 2 eligible people per
  shift") and **integrity constraints** (`:- assign(S,P),
  on_vacation(P,S).`, "discard any candidate world containing this") — so
  the program describes a whole space of candidate worlds and the solver
  hands back the ones that survive every constraint: an **answer set**.
  Not `ASP()` — a real, not hypothetical, collision with "average selling
  price" in finance spreadsheets, and the same naming-collision discipline
  `GO.1` already applies elsewhere in this file.
  - **The killer case, concretely:** staff scheduling, seating charts,
    resource allocation — "assign each person to a shift such that
    everyone works exactly 5 days, nobody works two in a row, every shift
    has at least 2 people, nobody's scheduled during their vacation days,
    total overtime is minimized." The thing people currently fight
    Excel's Solver add-in over, except Solver is a numeric black box with
    no way to ask why this answer and not another, and `OPTIMIZE` is built
    from the same named, inspectable facts as the other three. (Sudoku/
    N-Queens are the honest hello-world, not the pitch.)
  - **MVP** (`~weeks`, the heaviest MVP of the four): choice rules,
    integrity constraints, `DATALOG`'s stratified-negation rules reused
    as-is. The hard part is the solver, not the syntax — grounding
    (substituting concrete facts for variables, the same operation
    `DATALOG` already needs) followed by real backtracking search with
    constraint propagation, since unlike `DATALOG` this can't be solved
    by one monotone fixpoint pass. Returns the first answer set found, or
    an explicit "no valid answer set exists" — a first-class, auditable
    result, not a crash.
  - **Stretch** (`~weeks` more): all-answer-sets mode (spilled,
    `LIMIT`-capped — the count can be combinatorially huge), and
    `#minimize`/`#maximize` — turning "a valid schedule" into "the best
    one," the single most business-valuable mode this engine has.
  - **Ceiling** (`~months`, honestly research-grade): real conflict-driven
    search (CDCL-style, not naive backtracking) to stay responsive at
    real problem sizes inside a live calc engine; disjunctive rule heads
    for full theoretical ASP expressiveness, flagged as probably never
    needed for anything spreadsheet-shaped; an `EXPLAIN` showing which
    choices and constraints were binding — arguably more valuable here
    than for the other three, since "why is this the optimal schedule" is
    exactly what a human scheduler needs to trust this over Solver.
  - **Substrate relationship:** shares grounding with `DATALOG` (same
    range-to-facts machinery) and shares search/backtracking lineage with
    `PROLOG` (real combinatorial exploration, not a fixpoint) — sitting at
    the genuine intersection of both rather than a separate engine.
  - *Renamed `OPTIMIZE` on 2026-09-18, and re-planned: the build record
    below supersedes every sub-bullet here. Its family paragraph says why
    the name changed, why the naive search this scoping assumed (and the
    nine dissections that followed it) was retired on arithmetic, and why
    the search's shape is now measured before any of it is built.*

**Shared substrate, not four engines.** All four converge on the same
machinery at the ceiling: a recursive `PROLOG` query, a recursive `SQL`
`WITH` CTE, `DATALOG`'s fixpoint evaluation, and `OPTIMIZE`'s grounded search
are the same underlying computation wearing four different contracts
(unrestricted and possibly-nonterminating; recursive-and-relational;
restricted-and-guaranteed; generate-and-test), built from the same
indexed-relation primitives (hash join, group-by, projection, plus
`OPTIMIZE`'s own backtracking search over the grounded result). Building any
one's engine makes the others meaningfully cheaper — which is also the
argument for building `DATALOG` first: it is the smallest possible proof
of the shared bet, not a fourth thing competing for a turn — `OPTIMIZE` earns
that description honestly instead.

**The build record - moved here from BETA_ROADMAP.md on 2026-09-08.**

*The four entries above are the ORIGINAL scoping, kept as the trail. What
follows is the as-built record for the same four engines - every sub-item,
with the corrections to that original scoping noted inline where they were
made (for example: none of the four is a `function` or a `deflambda`; all are
add-in-native worksheet functions over `VLA_Relation.bas`). BETA_ROADMAP.md
now carries one summary paragraph per engine and points here.*

**Made explicit here, owner-asked, 2026-08-31, because it was previously only
  findable by reading `SQL`'s own dense decision paragraph in full:** the four
  engines in this section do NOT share one program-text representation.
  `DATALOG` and `PROLOG` do — both parse via `VLA.VlaReadForms`, VLA's own
  S-expression reader, into forms `VLA_Unify`/`VLA_Datalog` interpret, because
  textbook Datalog/Prolog have no surface syntax this audience already writes,
  so reusing VLA's own reader was free and right. `SQL` deliberately does NOT
  — `VLA_Sql.bas` has its own tokenizer and recursive-descent parser building
  its own AST (`NK_CMP`/`NK_ARITH`/`NK_AGG` node records, confirmed by grep:
  zero `VlaReadForms` calls anywhere in that file) — because real SQL syntax
  already exists in users' heads and a fifth invented S-expression dialect for
  it was considered and rejected (`SQL`'s own bullet, below, has the full
  "canonical surface syntax already exists → adopt it and pay the parser cost"
  reasoning). This is not an inconsistency to fix; it is the same rule applied
  twice with different inputs. **The one real question this asymmetry raises —
  does an eventual English→SQL phrasebook route have to detour through
  generated SQL TEXT, or can it target `VLA_Sql`'s own AST directly, the way
  English→`DATALOG`/`PROLOG` will target VLA forms directly — is already
  adjudicated, in `SQL`'s own bullet below, not reopened here:** phrasebook
  rows are recognizers, not generators (an English sentence is matched and
  parsed INTO a target representation; nothing requires emitting SQL text FROM
  a form), and the parse target stays genuinely open between canonical SQL
  text and `SQL.1`'s own engine-side expression tree until an actual
  English→SQL phrasebook row exists to need one — with canonical SQL text the
  recommended default specifically for auditability (a human-readable,
  pasteable intermediate), not because the cheaper direct-to-AST path is
  unavailable.

- ✅ **`SQL(table, query)`** — a relational query engine as a real worksheet
  function, prompted by `scripts/spreadsheet.lisp`'s own `SELECTFROM`/
  `SELECTROWS` (an Excel-native `LAMBDA`+`BYROW`+`FILTER` implementation)
  crashing on large tables. SQL.1–SQL.7 owner-tested live and committed (their
  own bullets below have the detail) - this section's own full SQL.1–SQL.7
  hydration is now shipped. **The one binding architectural decision,
  corrected from this item's original wording in `BETA_REARVIEW.md`:** neither
  `function` (an interpreter-local procedure, or an injected/exported VBA
  `Public Function` — not cell-callable without VBProject trust) nor
  `deflambda` (compiles to one native Excel `LAMBDA`, inheriting `BYROW`'s
  per-row recalculation ceiling regardless of how the query is worded) is the
  right shape. All four engines in this section are **add-in-native worksheet
  functions**, split as `VLA_Relation.bas` (the shared, DSL-ignorant substrate
  — Relation storage, `RelFromRange`, hash join, spilled-array output —
  corrected from this item's original "`VLA_Query.bas`" wording once `DATALOG`
  proved a single combined module would junk-drawer two unrelated concerns)
  plus one thin module per engine (`VLA_Datalog.bas`, shipped; future
  `VLA_Sql.bas`/`VLA_Prolog.bas`/`VLA_Solve.bas`) each owning only its own
  grammar and exposing its own `Public Function` — callable as `=SQL(...)`
  from any cell the moment the add-in loads, no VBProject trust, no export, no
  emitted code — using the standard high-performance pattern (one
  `Range.Value2` read into a Variant array, one native loop, one array
  write-back). SEC.1 Tier-0 by construction: pure read-and-return, no effects.
  Stated limit, same as `deflambda`'s: an exported standalone workbook using
  `=SQL()` needs the add-in present. **Three cell-facing spellings fixed now,
  before any engine code, because SD-4 freezes them on first use:** every
  engine returns a spilled 2D array, header row first, matching `SELECTROWS`'s
  existing shape — never a scalar, a JSON blob, or a lazy handle; query text
  is locale-invariant (`.` decimal separator, ISO 8601 dates, `,` argument
  separator) regardless of the user's Excel locale, decided now rather than
  inherited by accident from EN.2/EN.3's later policy; and `PROLOG`/`OPTIMIZE`
  specifically must enforce a hard resolution-step budget, refusing by name
  past the ceiling, because an in-cell UDF has no `DoEvents` path (IN.14's
  cancellation is interpreter-loop-only) and an unbounded backtracking search
  freezes Excel with only Esc/Ctrl+Break as the user's exit. **Grammar
  surface, decided 2026-08-29 (owner call, SD-4 freeze-on-first-use):** query
  text is real SQL, not a fourth S-expression dialect. The deciding rule:
  *when a canonical surface syntax already exists in the intended users'
  heads, adopt it and pay the parser cost; invent syntax only when there is
  nothing to adopt.* `DATALOG`'s S-expression choice and this one are the same
  rule applied twice, not an inconsistency — textbook Datalog has no surface
  this audience already writes (so `VlaReadForms` reuse was free and right),
  while SQL emphatically does, and the specimen behind this whole tranche
  asked for *SQL, the language, by name*; SQL text is also pastable from
  everywhere the owner already knows it and readable by any auditor, the
  auditability-before-procedural-power stance applied to query text itself.
  The cost — a real tokenizer plus recursive-descent parser instead of a
  reader reuse — is bounded exactly the way `datalog-compound-term` bounded
  `DATALOG`: a named, frozen subset (each SQL.X below adds its own keywords
  and nothing else), with everything outside it refused by name at parse time
  (`sql-unsupported-keyword` and kin), never guessed. One surface only — a
  dual/auto-detected S-expression spelling was considered and rejected as
  freezing two grammars, two test surfaces, and two refusal vocabularies
  forever for one engine. **Two refinements, owner-raised 2026-08-29, same
  session:** *(1)* the English-phrasebook end-goal (grammar `{slot:type}` rows
  matching English query sentences against queries in all four DSLs — the
  `PROLOG` item's own stated framing) was weighed as the strongest argument
  for S-expressions and does not reverse this decision, with the pipeline's
  direction stated precisely (owner correction, same session): phrasebook rows
  are *recognizers*, not generators — an English sentence is matched and
  parsed *into* a target query representation; nothing here requires SQL to be
  *emitted* by grammar forms unless Frazaro's own English↔VLA bidirectionality
  promise is ever extended to this tranche (rendering a query back as English,
  or displaying canonical SQL for a matched sentence, would need a
  pretty-printer — emission — a separate decision deferred until that promise
  is actually invoked here, not bought now). The parse *target* is likewise
  open until a phrasebook row exists to need one — canonical SQL text, or the
  engine-side expression tree SQL.1's parser builds anyway (SD-4 froze what
  humans type into cells, not the module's internal seams, so an internal
  target is not a second public grammar) — with canonical SQL text the
  recommended default when the time comes: the translation's intermediate is
  then auditor-visible, user-editable, and pastable, the
  auditability-before-procedural-power stance applied to translation itself,
  at the cost of template quoting-discipline plus a trivial re-parse. Either
  way the decisive point stands: matching English into a deterministic target
  is equally cheap whichever representation the target is, so the phrasebook
  goal is surface-neutral and the adoption/pasteability argument decides.
  *(2)* One dialect, pinned: mixing SQL dialects invalidates all of them de
  facto, so the frozen subset names a single reference dialect for tie-breaks
  (string concatenation, `''` quote-escaping, identifier quoting — date
  literals already settled by the locale-invariance freeze above). The
  subset's existing spellings (`LIMIT` not `TOP`, `<>`, single-quoted strings)
  already lean SQLite-shaped, and SQLite is the recommended pin — the
  most-pasted tutorial dialect, and the one whose in-process, single-user,
  no-server philosophy this engine shares — final pin an owner call at SQL.1's
  first grammar line, per SD-4. Hydrated below into SQL.1–SQL.7, ordered in
  the house metametamacro style — microscopes before dissections: each item
  builds machinery a later item consumes, never the reverse.
  - ✅ **Single-table `SELECT`/`WHERE` — the parser and evaluator microscopes,
    SQL.1 (MVP).** Owner-tested live and committed. Tokenizer plus
    recursive-descent parser over this item's frozen subset: `SELECT col, col`
    / `SELECT *`, `FROM` naming exactly one passed table, `WHERE` with
    `=`/`<>`/`<`/`<=`/`>`/`>=`, `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`, parentheses, real precedence
    — a proper expression tree (`VLA_Sql.bas`), per `BETA_REARVIEW.md`'s own
    correction that `EXTRACTOPERATOR`-style string-`FIND` heuristics cannot
    handle precedence or nesting. Two microscopes every later item consumes
    get built here and only here: the parser skeleton with its refuse-by-name
    discipline (`sql-unsupported-keyword` and kin; cell errors as `"#SQL!
    ..."`, `DATALOG`'s own precedent) and the scalar expression evaluator
    (`EvalScalar`/`EvalBool`) — SQL.2's computed columns, SQL.3's residual
    `ON` conditions, and SQL.4's `HAVING` are all this one evaluator pointed
    at different rows. DATALOG.4 (above) has since consumed this evaluator's
    own mechanical core rather than growing a twin, though not
    `EvalScalar`/`EvalBool` themselves (SQL's own AST-walking shape doesn't
    fit DATALOG's flat two-operand atoms) — the truly shared, DSL-ignorant
    part (compare/compute given already-typed operands) moved into
    `VLA_Relation.bas`, and `EvalBool`'s own `NK_CMP` case now calls that
    shared function directly; DATALOG.4's own bullet has the full mechanism
    and the one genuine divergence (numeric-vs-text policy, necessarily
    different per engine). Number literals parse via VBA's `Val()`, not
    `CDbl`, since `Val` alone is genuinely locale-invariant in VBA (`CDbl`
    respects the user's own regional decimal separator) — the `.`-always
    freeze made real, not just stated. New substrate this engine forces that
    `DATALOG` never needed: named-column resolution — `DATALOG` is
    deliberately positional, SQL is name-based, so `VLA_Relation.bas` grows
    `RangeColumnNames` (a folded/original column-name map, column names folded
    once through `VLA_Identity.Fold` — `BETA_REARVIEW.md`'s law, not a second
    `LCase`, which would reintroduce the Turkish-`I` locale bug the neutrality
    audit already flags) and `TableArgResolve` (`VLA_Datalog.bas`'s own
    `TableArgName` hoisted here as a message-agnostic resolver the moment a
    second engine needed it — the substrate/engine split doing its job; each
    engine's own thin wrapper turns its category code back into that engine's
    own wording, so refusal vocabulary stays exactly as separate as it already
    was). **A real correctness catch made while building this, not while
    testing it:** SQL rows are a *bag* (a table may legitimately contain
    duplicate rows, and querying it must return every one), while
    `VLA_Relation`'s own `Relation`/`RelFromRange` is a *set* (`RelTryAdd`
    silently absorbs an already-seen tuple — correct for Datalog facts, wrong
    for SQL) — reusing `RelFromRange` directly for SQL's own row reading would
    have silently dropped duplicate source rows. `VLA_Relation.RangeToRows` is
    the bag-preserving counterpart built instead, sharing `SourceToArray`'s
    own header-stripping logic but never wrapping results in a deduping
    `Relation`. Matched rows collect into a manually-doubled buffer
    (`BufAdd`), never per-row `ReDim Preserve` (the O(n²) trap this whole item
    exists to kill). **One signature decision made, not the item's own literal
    title:** the shipped UDF is `SQL(queryText, ParamArray tables())`, not
    `SQL(table, query)` as titled above — VBA requires a `ParamArray` to be a
    function's own last parameter (a hard language rule `DATALOG`'s own
    signature already relies on), and SQL.3's future `JOIN` will need
    *multiple* tables, so this is the one shape that can grow to that later
    without ever breaking a formula written against SQL.1; the title's own
    `table, query` order was a mnemonic, not a freeze. SQL.1's own stated MVP
    limits: exactly one table for now (`sql-needs-exactly-one-table` — `JOIN`
    is SQL.3, not here); the table argument must be a real Excel Table
    (`sql-table-needs-real-table`) since SQL fundamentally needs column names
    DATALOG's own positional convention never required; `FROM` must name the
    same table actually passed in (`sql-from-table-mismatch`), `DATALOG`'s own
    table-predicate-naming discipline reused rather than a new one invented.
    Real SQLite syntax is honored, not just "SQL-in-general": both comment
    forms (`--` to end of line, `/* ... */`) are skipped like whitespace and
    exactly one trailing `;` is tolerated (refusing, not truncating, anything
    after it) — both ordinary artifacts of a query actually copied from a real
    tool, checked deliberately after the owner asked whether the dialect pin
    was genuinely being honored rather than cherry-picked; that same audit
    also confirmed string-data comparison stays case-SENSITIVE
    (`vbBinaryCompare`, SQLite's own default — no silent `NOCASE`) while
    identifier matching stays case-insensitive (`VLA_Identity.Fold`, SQLite's
    own default there too) - getting those two backwards would have been the
    exact cherry-pick being asked about. Tests: `VLA_Tests_Query.TestSql`
    (pure — a hand-built column-name/row pair, including a deliberate
    duplicate row proving bag semantics survive, an `AND`/`OR` precedence case
    and its parenthesized override, and the comment/semicolon tolerance) and
    `TestSqlHostTable` (host-required — a real `ListObject`, the actual
    `=SQL(...)` worksheet function called directly). **Two real bugs
    live-caught, neither by the pure suite:** *(1)* a grammar defect, not a
    wiring slip — `'(' expr ')'` was reachable both as a complete boolean
    expression and as a scalar `primary` (a comparison's own operand), so `NOT
    (dept = 'eng')` parsed the whole parenthesized group as if it were one
    scalar value and then went hunting for a comparison operator after a group
    that had already completed one internally; fixed by moving `'('` handling
    out of `ParsePrimary` entirely and into `ParseNotExpr` (the boolean level)
    — SQL.1 has no arithmetic that would ever need a parenthesized scalar, so
    every `'('` is unambiguously a boolean group. *(2)* `RangeColumnNames`
    (`VLA_Relation.bas`) had `Dim pair As New Collection` inside its own
    column loop — this exact codebase's own already-documented trap (`As New`
    only auto-instantiates when Nothing, never again after the first
    iteration) — so every column's own name pair was really the SAME
    ever-growing Collection object, and `colMap` ended up with exactly one
    usable key. Live-caught because `SELECT *` never exercises `colMap` at all
    (it reads columns positionally), so the pure suite's own `SELECT *` check
    — which only verified the FIRST header — passed clean; only an explicit
    `WHERE` column reference surfaced it. Fixed with the standard `Set`
    discipline, and the `SELECT *` test strengthened to check every header,
    not a sample.
  - ✅ **Computed `SELECT` expressions, `AS` aliases, `DISTINCT`, SQL.2.**
    Owner-tested live (`TestDSLs` 104/104, plus live `=SQL(...)` cell-formula
    checks: `DISTINCT` collapsing repeated department values, the
    missing-alias refusal, and the one documented left-operand-paren limit
    reproducing its predicted error text exactly) and committed. The evaluator
    already existed (SQL.1); this points it at the projection list instead of
    only the filter — `SELECT salary * 1.1 AS raised` cost real grammar, not
    zero machinery as first estimated: SQL.1 had no arithmetic operators at
    all (`+`/`-`/`/` weren't even tokenized; SQL.1's own `*` existed only for
    `SELECT *`), so this item grew a genuine precedence hierarchy — `addExpr`
    (`+`/`-`, left-associative) over `mulExpr` (`*`/`/`, left-associative)
    over `primary` (column/number/string, unary `+`/`-`, or a parenthesized
    `addExpr`) — with `NK_ARITH` joining the AST and `ParseComparison`'s own
    operands now calling `ParseAddExpr` instead of a bare `primary`, so `WHERE
    salary * 1.1 > 100000` works with no parens needed — one evaluator,
    pointed at both the projection list and the filter, per this item's own
    words, not two. `AS` matters beyond convenience: output-column names are
    what `GROUP BY` and `ORDER BY` later refer back to, so aliasing lands
    before both consumers exist — realized as a parse-time requirement, not
    just a convenience: a computed (non-bare-column) `SELECT` item with no
    `AS` of its own is refused (`sql-computed-column-needs-alias`), a scoping
    call made this session rather than following real SQL's own
    auto-name-from-expression-text convention, which would invent a name this
    engine's own "refuse rather than silently guess" culture argues against
    when later consumers need to refer back to it reliably. `DISTINCT` needed
    no new substrate at all: `VLA_Relation.RelNew`/`RelTryAdd` (already
    `Public`, already Mac-fallback aware) reused directly as a ready-made
    case-sensitive whole-row dedup set for the projected output rows. **One
    real grammar hazard navigated, not discovered live this time:** SQL.1's
    own live-caught fix (`'(' expr ')'` must never be reachable as both a
    complete boolean expression and a scalar operand in the same grammar)
    meant SQL.2's own new `'(' addExpr ')'` handling had to be added to
    `ParsePrimary` specifically — reached only from a comparison's own operand
    or a SELECT-list item, never from `ParseNotExpr`'s own top-level dispatch,
    which still claims a leading `'('` for boolean grouping first,
    unconditionally, exactly as before. Traced case-by-case before writing any
    code, this resolves every position except one, named as a deliberate,
    documented limit rather than solved with lookahead machinery out of this
    item's own `~days` scope: a comparison's own LEFT operand can never itself
    start with `'('` at the very top of a condition (`WHERE (a + b) > 10` is
    refused — `ParseNotExpr` always wins that race — not silently misparsed);
    every other position (a comparison's own RIGHT operand, anything nested
    inside an already-committed arithmetic expression, and any SELECT-list
    item) is unaffected. `ComputeArithmetic` (`VLA_Relation.bas`, hoisted by
    DATALOG.4) gets its second real caller here, proving that hoist out —
    SQL's own numeric-ness policy for arithmetic stays STRICT
    (`ValueIsNumericType` alone), the identical policy `EvalBool`'s own
    comparison case already used, never DATALOG's own more lenient
    numeric-looking-string policy. Tests: `VLA_Tests_Query.TestSql`, pure
    (SQL.2 needed no new host-specific mechanism, unlike SQL.1's own
    real-`ListObject` needs for named columns) — a computed column with its
    own alias (value-checked), `AS` renaming a bare column, an un-aliased
    computed column refused, `DISTINCT` on one column/on `*`/combined with
    `WHERE` (proving `WHERE` filters before `DISTINCT`, not after),
    `*`-before-`+` precedence and its parenthesized override, unary minus,
    `WHERE` reusing the same arithmetic grammar with no parens needed,
    division by zero and a non-numeric operand refused, and the one documented
    left-operand-paren limit confirmed as a clean refusal.
  - ✅ **`INNER JOIN ... ON`, SQL.3.** Owner-tested live (`TestDSLs` 134/134,
    plus three live `=SQL(...)` cell-formula checks: a two-table JOIN with
    qualified columns, an ambiguous-unqualified-column refusal, and an
    unsupported-join-kind refusal) and committed. `~days`–`~weeks`. Reuses
    `VLA_Relation.RelJoin`'s hash join directly (`BETA_REARVIEW.md`'s standing
    law: always a hash join, `Dictionary` built on the smaller side —
    nested-loop join is not an acceptable implementation at any table size).
    The parser splits each `ON` into equi-conditions (fed to the hash join as
    keys) plus residual non-equi conditions (evaluated as a post-join filter
    through SQL.1's evaluator — zero new evaluation code). Qualified column
    names (`Employees.id`) enter the name-resolution map here, since two
    joined tables can collide; multiple `JOIN`s fold left-to-right. `LEFT
    JOIN` deliberately deferred: `DATALOG`'s `not` already proves the
    substrate can express the anti-join half, but it is a dissection, not a
    microscope — nothing downstream needs it, so it waits for a real query
    that does.
  - ✅ **`GROUP BY` / aggregates / `HAVING`, SQL.4.** Owner-tested live
    (`TestDSLs` 154/154, plus four live `=SQL(...)` cell-formula checks) and
    committed. `COUNT`/`SUM`/`MIN`/`MAX`/`AVG`. The third appearance of
    grouping in this codebase (DATALOG.2's `count`/`sum`, SQL.2's `DISTINCT`),
    generalized rather than reinvented: `VLA_Relation.RelGroupBy` is the
    shared grouping kernel (group-key-building plus per-group accumulators,
    over already-resolved column positions), leaving DATALOG.2's own
    bound/unbound-variable consistency checking exactly where it is (real
    Datalog unification-lite semantics, not generic grouping). Grammar
    additions: an aggregate call (`COUNT`/`SUM`/`MIN`/`MAX`/`AVG` immediately
    followed by `(`) is a new scalar AST node (`NK_AGG`), parsed inside
    `ParsePrimary`; `GROUP BY` is deliberately restricted to bare/qualified
    COLUMN items only, not a general expression (the grouped row only carries
    GROUP BY key values plus aggregate results forward, so a computed GROUP BY
    item would have no sound re-evaluation path); `HAVING` reuses
    `ParseOrExpr`, the same boolean grammar `WHERE`/`ON` already use. `HAVING`
    is SQL.1's evaluator run once more over the grouped relation — `EvalBool`
    needed zero changes; `EvalScalar` gained one new `Case NK_AGG`, the same
    kind of addition SQL.2's own `NK_ARITH` case already was. Ungrouped
    aggregates (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM T WHERE ...`) return their one-row
    answer even over zero matching rows, the same "an empty result is a real
    answer, not an error" stance DATALOG.2 already took — `COUNT`/`SUM` are
    real zeros there; `MIN`/`MAX`/`AVG` have no defined answer over zero rows
    and are refused by name (no NULL representation exists anywhere in this
    engine) rather than inventing one. `SELECT *` is refused whenever a query
    groups or aggregates at all; every non-aggregate `SELECT` item must
    structurally match a `GROUP BY` item or be refused
    (`sql-select-item-not-grouped`). Tests: `VLA_Tests_Query.TestSql` (pure —
    grouping/aggregates/HAVING over a single table, all five aggregate
    functions, the zero-rows COUNT/SUM-vs-MIN/MAX/AVG split, and the full set
    of new parse-time refusals), `TestSqlJoin` (pure — `GROUP BY` over a
    joined row set), `TestSqlHostTable` (host-required — `GROUP BY` +
    `COUNT`/`SUM` + `HAVING` over a live two-table `JOIN`, through the actual
    `=SQL(...)` worksheet function).
  - ✅ **`ORDER BY` / `LIMIT`, SQL.5.** Owner-tested live (`TestDSLs` 170/170,
    plus a live `=SQL(...)` cell-formula check catching a real
    resolution-scope bug, fixed and re-verified) and committed. The one
    deliberately-late dissection: nothing downstream consumes ordering, so
    this item floats — sequenced here not because anything needs it but
    because it is pure presentation. Needs no new AST node kind and no
    tokenizer change at all - `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT` items never re-enter the
    scalar/boolean evaluator. `ORDER BY` item ::= (position | column
    name/alias) `[ASC | DESC]`, resolved by trying TWO namespaces in order:
    this query's own OUTPUT header list first (a 1-based position, or a
    SELECT-list item's own alias/bare-column name — an output alias wins over
    a same-named source column, real SQL's own rule), then, only when a name
    matches nothing there, falling back to the same `colMap` `WHERE`/`HAVING`
    already resolve bare column names against (a real table column, or a
    `GROUP BY` key/aggregate for a grouped query, that was never re-selected
    at all — real SQL's, and specifically SQLite's, own ordinary allowance).
    **One real correction made live, not caught by the pure suite first:** v1
    resolved `ORDER BY` against the output header list *only*, reasoning by
    direct analogy from `GROUP BY`'s own column-only restriction (a
    transformed row's missing columns have no sound re-evaluation path) — the
    owner's own very first live check, `ORDER BY dept` over a query that only
    `SELECT`ed name, was wrongly refused; every real SQL engine just sorts by
    it. The analogy didn't actually transfer: `GROUP BY`'s concern was a
    transformed row having *no value at all* to sort by, but `ORDER BY`'s own
    row loop still has the full source (or grouped) row in hand when it runs,
    `colMap` already resolving names against it for `WHERE`/`HAVING` — so
    falling back to it costs nothing new. An out-of-range position or a name
    matching zero or more than one candidate (in whichever namespace resolves
    it) is refused by name, mirroring SQL.3's own `sql-ambiguous-column`
    discipline. Multi-key, `ASC`/`DESC` (default `ASC`), one stable sort
    routine written once (VBA has no native array sort) - a merge sort over
    row *indices*, kept entirely separate from `DISTINCT`'s own dedup (which
    must only ever see real output values, never an unselected `ORDER BY` key)
    - each key's own comparison reusing `VLA_Relation.CompareValues` directly,
    the identical numeric-vs-text policy `WHERE`/`HAVING` already use. `LIMIT`
    is a plain non-negative integer literal, a row-count cutoff applied after
    the sort - `LIMIT 0` is a real, valid zero-row result, not an error.
    Tests: `VLA_Tests_Query.TestSql` (pure - ascending/descending, a dedicated
    stability check via a genuine three-way tie, multi-key, ordinal position,
    ordering by a column outside the SELECT list (both an ordinary and a
    grouped query), `LIMIT` with and without `ORDER BY`, `LIMIT 0`, and the
    full set of new refusals), `TestSqlJoin` (pure - `ORDER BY` over a joined
    row set), `TestSqlHostTable` (host-required - `ORDER BY ... DESC LIMIT 2`
    through the actual `=SQL(...)` worksheet function).
  - ✅ **`UNION` / `UNION ALL` / `INTERSECT` / `EXCEPT`, SQL.6.** `~days`.
    Owner-tested live (`TestDSLs` 184/184, plus twelve live `=SQL(...)`
    cell-formula checks against fresh, hand-built Tables independent of the
    test harness: dedup, concatenation, cross-table `UNION`, `INTERSECT`,
    non-symmetric `EXCEPT` both directions, the arity-mismatch refusal,
    `INTERSECT`-binds-tighter precedence, `ORDER BY ... LIMIT` on the combined
    result, the compound `ORDER BY` refusing to fall back to an un-selected
    source column, the SAME non-compound query still getting SQL.5's own
    source-column fallback unchanged, and the first branch's own alias naming
    the whole result) and committed. Column-count compatibility checked and
    refused by name (`sql-set-op-column-mismatch`), post-evaluation (a `SELECT
    *` branch's own arity is only known once it has actually run). `UNION ALL`
    is concatenation; the other three are SQL.2's whole-row key-hashing
    applied again (dedup, membership, anti-membership — `EXCEPT` is `not`'s
    anti-join wearing SQL clothes) — zero new `VLA_Relation.bas` substrate,
    `RelNew`/`RelTryAdd`/`RelContainsTuple` reused directly. A NEW grammar
    layer (`ParseCompoundQuery`/`SqlRunCompound`, `VLA_Sql.bas`), not an
    extension of the existing one: real SQLite precedence (`INTERSECT` binds
    tighter than `UNION`/`UNION ALL`/`EXCEPT`, which are left-associative with
    each other), mirroring `ParseAddExpr`/`ParseMulExpr`'s own
    precedence-climbing shape. Each branch is sliced out of the original query
    text (by character offset) and re-run through the EXISTING, unchanged
    `SqlRunJoin` — so `SqlRunJoin`/`SqlRun`/every SQL.1–SQL.5 test needed zero
    changes, and a non-compound query through the new `SqlRunCompound` entry
    point degenerates to exactly `SqlRunJoin`, SQL.5's own `ORDER BY`
    source-column fallback included. `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT` trail the whole
    compound query exactly once, resolved only against the combined OUTPUT
    columns (no per-branch source-colMap fallback survives combining two
    branches — named, not silently half-working). The first branch's own
    headers name the whole compound result. **One real refusal live-caught,
    not by the pure suite first:** the live test's own first-drafted query
    paired a bare literal (`'total' AS Dept`) with `COUNT(*)` in a SELECT list
    with no `GROUP BY` at all — a shape real SQL permits (a constant needs no
    grouping) but this engine's own already-shipped SQL.4 rule does not (every
    non-aggregate `SELECT` item must structurally match a `GROUP BY` item; a
    literal isn't a column and matches nothing) — fixed by reshaping the live
    test's own query, not by loosening SQL.4's rule after the fact. Tests:
    `VLA_Tests_Query.TestSqlSetOps` (pure — all four operators, the
    arity-mismatch refusal, `INTERSECT`-binds-tighter precedence proven with
    data where the two groupings diverge, and the non-compound
    backward-compatibility promise proven directly), `TestSqlHostTable`
    (host-required — a live `UNION ALL` combining a `JOIN`+`GROUP BY` branch
    with a plain-table aggregate branch, `ORDER BY`'d, through the actual
    `=SQL(...)` worksheet function). Sequenced before CTEs for one
    load-bearing reason: `UNION ALL` is the exact ingredient a recursive
    `WITH` is made of, so SQL.7 arrives with its hardest-looking piece already
    on the shelf.
  - ✅ **`WITH` CTEs, then recursive `WITH`, SQL.7 — the convergence proof.**
    `~weeks`. Owner-tested live (`TestDSLs` 198/198, plus seventeen live
    `=SQL(...)` cell-formula checks spanning non-recursive `WITH` basics,
    namespace/shadowing, the already-impossible-so-no-new-code
    derived-table/correlated-subquery cases, the recursive convergence proof
    itself over a live table plus a self-bounding `WHERE`-terminated counter
    CTE, a recursive CTE's own output consumed by `GROUP BY` in the main
    query, mixed recursive/non-recursive CTEs in one `WITH RECURSIVE` clause,
    an empty-base CTE resolving to a real zero rather than an error, and every
    named shape refusal) and committed. Non-recursive `WITH` first: named
    subresults, each a full compound query (SQL.6's own grammar, unchanged)
    evaluated in written order and registered as a synthetic table joining the
    `FROM`/`JOIN` namespace of every LATER `cte` and the final query —
    deliberately the *only* subquery mechanism this engine gets: derived
    tables (`FROM (SELECT ...)`) and correlated subqueries needed no new
    refusal at all, already structurally impossible in this grammar (no
    position ever accepts a `(` `SELECT` `)`), confirmed and named rather than
    left an unexamined accident. A same-named real table is simply shadowed
    (real SQL's own rule), true for free from `SqlRunJoin`'s own existing
    table-registration order, no special-casing. Then recursive `WITH
    RECURSIVE name AS (base UNION ALL step)`: examined closely before writing
    any code, not assumed — `VLA_Datalog`'s own fixpoint runner is hard-coded
    to Datalog's own atom/body-item representation and can't be called
    directly (VBA has no first-class function value to hand it a SQL step as a
    generic callback either), so what's genuinely reused is the semi-naive
    ALGORITHM shape itself (round 1 = full base; round N>1 = the step
    evaluated against ONLY round N-1's own delta; stop the moment a round
    contributes zero new rows; a named round ceiling — `SQL_CTE_MAX_ROUNDS`,
    matching `VLA_Datalog`'s own `MAX_ROUNDS` value, 10000 — as the safety
    valve, never a normal exit) — achieved entirely through `SqlRunJoin`'s own
    existing table-substitution seam (each round's own delta is just another
    synthetic table under the CTE's own name), no new evaluation machinery at
    all. One deliberately narrow recursive shape supported and named: `base
    UNION ALL step`, neither side itself a further compound expression, the
    base referencing itself never and the step referencing itself exactly once
    — every other shape (a self-reference with no `RECURSIVE` keyword, a
    self-reference inside `INTERSECT`/`EXCEPT`, a self-referencing base, a
    step self-joined against the recursive CTE, `ORDER BY`/`LIMIT` inside the
    recursive definition itself) refused by name. This is the item that cashes
    in the section's own claim that a recursive `WITH` CTE and `DATALOG`'s
    fixpoint are the same computation wearing different contracts — the
    shared-substrate bet, proven a second time, verified with a hand-checked
    transitive closure over a 4-node chain (exactly 6 rows, not more) that
    would catch a "used the full total instead of the delta" bug via row count
    alone. Tests: `VLA_Tests_Query.TestSqlCte` (pure — multiple CTEs
    referencing each other, shadowing, the derived-table/correlated-subquery
    non-issue, every named recursive-shape refusal, and the convergence proof
    itself), `TestSqlHostTable` (host-required — a live recursive `WITH` over
    a real `Employees`/manager Table through `=SQL(...)`, the same "everything
    transitively under this row" shape `BETA_REARVIEW.md`'s own `DATALOG`
    motivating example already used, now answered by `SQL` directly).
  - ⬜ **SQL.8 — `LEFT`/`RIGHT`/`FULL` `OUTER JOIN`, `CROSS JOIN`, and table
    aliasing (`AS`) for self-joins.** Two real, owner-named gaps sitting at
    the exact same grammar boundary, both already refused BY NAME rather than
    falling through to a generic error: `RefuseUnsupportedJoinKind`
    (`VLA_Sql.bas`) raises `sql-outer-join-not-supported` for
    `left`/`right`/`full`/`outer`/`cross`, checked wherever a `JOIN` keyword
    could legally start; `sql-duplicate-join-table` separately refuses naming
    the same table twice across `FROM`/`JOIN`, naming self-joins specifically
    as the reason a table needs its own alias. SQL.3's own header already
    sketches the outer-join half honestly: `DATALOG`'s `not` proves the
    substrate can express an anti-join (keep the left row when no matching
    right row exists), so this is real work, not unknown territory — "it is a
    dissection, not a microscope; nothing downstream needs it, so it waits for
    a real query that does." That real query is the README's own staffing
    example's natural next question ("which shifts have NO one who can cover
    them" is exactly a `LEFT JOIN ... WHERE right.key IS NULL` shape once
    `SQL.9`'s own `IS NULL` exists). Table aliasing threads a new `AS name`
    binding through `MakeJoinRec`/name resolution ahead of the join itself —
    smaller than the outer-join half, genuinely useful alone (two SELECTs from
    the same Table under different names) even before `LEFT JOIN` ships.
    `~weeks`.
  - ⬜ **SQL.9 — `NULL`, `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL`, and three-valued
    `WHERE`/`HAVING` logic.** A real, currently undocumented gap, not merely
    an unbuilt feature: no `sql-` message anywhere in `VLA_Messages.bas`
    mentions `NULL`, and a blank cell inside an otherwise non-blank row is not
    refused — it flows straight through `RangeToRows` (`VLA_Relation.bas`) as
    a raw Excel `Empty` variant into `EvalScalar`/`EvalBool` (`VLA_Sql.bas`),
    with no defined comparison, arithmetic, or aggregate behavior once it gets
    there; today's answer is whatever VBA's own `Empty`-coercion rules happen
    to produce, not a chosen one. Real SQL's `NULL` is foundational, not
    decorative — `=`/`<`/`>` against a `NULL` is `UNKNOWN`, not `TRUE` or
    `FALSE` (excluding the row from `WHERE`/`HAVING` either way);
    `COUNT`/`SUM`/`AVG`/`MIN`/`MAX` all skip a `NULL` operand rather than
    erroring or coercing it into `0`; `IS NULL`/`IS NOT NULL` are the only
    correct way to test for it (`= NULL` is a classic beginner bug real
    engines warn about, worth refusing by name here too). `COALESCE`/`NULLIF`
    are the two ordinary companions once the concept exists. Hooks into the
    same `EvalScalar`/`EvalBool` pair `SQL.9`'s siblings below extend.
    `~weeks`. *Blocks:* the anti-join idiom `SQL.8`'s own header names (`LEFT
    JOIN ... WHERE right.key IS NULL`).
  - ⬜ **SQL.10 — `LIKE`, `IN (...)`, `BETWEEN`, and `CASE WHEN`.** Four
    ordinary SQL conveniences with zero presence in the grammar today — none
    has its own named refusal; each currently falls into the generic
    `sql-unsupported-keyword` bucket (`'{keyword}' isn't part of SQL's own
    supported subset yet (SELECT DISTINCT/FROM/WHERE, AS, AND/OR/NOT, = <> <
    <= > >=, + - * /, parentheses)`), which is honest but not diagnostically
    pointed at any one of these four the way `sql-outer-join-not-supported` is
    pointed at outer joins. `LIKE`/`IN`/`BETWEEN` are new cases at
    `ParseComparison`'s own precedence level (`VLA_Sql.bas`) — the same slot
    `=`/`<>`/`<`/`<=`/`>`/`>=` already occupy — `LIKE`'s own `%`/`_` wildcards
    translated to a small anchored-match routine (never a regex engine; SQL's
    own frozen-subset philosophy argues for the narrowest thing that satisfies
    real SQL semantics), `IN (...)` as sugar over an OR-chain of equality,
    `BETWEEN lo AND hi` as sugar over two comparisons ANDed. `CASE WHEN ...
    THEN ... ELSE ... END` is a new primary-expression form in `ParsePrimary`,
    evaluated through the same `EvalScalar` every other expression already is.
    `~weeks`.
  - ⬜ **SQL.11 — subqueries: scalar, `IN (SELECT ...)`, and `EXISTS`/`NOT
    EXISTS`.** The one remaining structural gap against ordinary relational
    SQL, not a ceiling item — a subquery is still a single, non-recursive
    `SELECT` (recursion already has its own named, terminating mechanism,
    `SQL.7`'s `WITH RECURSIVE`), so nothing here threatens the frozen subset's
    own termination guarantee. Three shapes, in order of how much new
    machinery each needs: a scalar subquery (`WHERE Salary > (SELECT
    AVG(Salary) FROM Staff)`) reuses the existing single-`SELECT` pipeline
    wholesale, feeding one resulting value into `EvalScalar`; `IN (SELECT
    ...)` needs the subquery's own result column hashed the same way `SQL.3`'s
    own join key already is (`VLA_Relation.RelJoin`'s hash-join law extends
    naturally — an `IN` subquery is a semi-join, `NOT IN` its anti-join twin,
    the same shape `SQL.8`'s own outer-join half already needs); `EXISTS`/`NOT
    EXISTS` is the same semi-/anti-join test with the subquery's own SELECT
    list ignored (existence only). A genuinely open, owner-decidable question
    this item should answer rather than assume: whether a CORRELATED subquery
    (one referencing a column from the enclosing query) is in scope for v1, or
    deferred as its own follow-on the way `SQL.3` deferred outer joins — an
    uncorrelated subquery is strictly simpler (evaluate once, reuse the
    result) and may be the right MVP cut. `~weeks`–`~months`. *Pays into:*
    `SQL.9`'s own `NULL` semantics, since `NOT IN (SELECT ...)` against a
    subquery result containing `NULL` is real SQL's own most notorious
    surprise (the whole `NOT IN` returns no rows at all) and deserves a named
    test, not a silent trap.
  - ✅ **SQL.12 — `GROUP BY` groups text exactly, as SQLite does.** Minted
    2026-09-29, the owner's call, from `DATALOG.16`'s audit, and built,
    tested live and committed in the same pass. **The defect, read from the
    code:** `RelGroupBy`
    (`VLA_Relation.bas`, `SQL.4`'s kernel) kept all four of its maps - the
    groups seen, their key values, their counts and each aggregate's running
    value - in `VLA_Runtime.VlaDictNew()`, which compares without case, so
    `SELECT Name, COUNT(*) FROM People GROUP BY Name` over `Bob`, `bob` and
    `Bob` answered one group, `Bob 3`. The same engine's `DISTINCT`, `=`
    and `JOIN` tell the two apart, and `VLA_Sql.bas`'s own header pins
    SQLite: "case-sensitive string DATA comparison (vbBinaryCompare, never
    a silent NOCASE)", with `VlaDict` for "identifier lookups only, never
    row data". SQLite's `BINARY` collation groups the way its `=` compares.
    Not a separate, deliberate rule: `RelGroupBy`'s header says it
    generalises `DATALOG.2`'s grouping, and it carried the same `VlaDict`
    over. **The fix:** its four maps are `DATALOG.16`'s exact map -
    twenty-eight mechanical renames in `RelGroupBy` and `AccumulateAggValue`,
    nothing else changed - and `VLA_Relation.bas` now calls `VLA_Runtime`
    nowhere. **Pins:** `TestSqlGroupCase` (new, pure, 4): two groups, Bob
    first; each counts and sums its own rows (Bob 2 and 11, bob 1 and 5);
    `MIN` and `MAX` read their own group (Bob 1 to 10, bob 5 to 5); and
    `DISTINCT`, which always compared exactly, agrees. **A named limit, left
    for `SQL.10`:** an aggregate's signature carries a string literal as
    written and is a key in two `VlaDict`s - `ComputeGroupedRows`' `aggSeen`
    and the grouped colMap, which holds column names too - so, read from
    the code, `MAX('Bob')` beside `MAX('bob')` would share one slot and both
    show `Bob`. Contrived while only a bare literal can sit inside an
    aggregate; `SQL.10`'s `CASE WHEN` makes it ordinary
    (`SUM(CASE WHEN Name = 'Bob' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)`), so close it there, by
    keying a literal's text in a form no fold can merge. Named at
    `AggSignature`. **LIVE, 2026-09-29, step 7 of
    `archive/datalog16_live_steps.md`:** over a `PeopleD16` Table holding
    `Bob 10`, `bob 5` and `Bob 1`, `GROUP BY Name` spilled `Name n s` /
    `Bob 2 11` / `bob 1 5`, as predicted - one row, `Bob 3 16`, before.
    `~hours`
  - **Stated non-goals and ceiling, unchanged from `BETA_REARVIEW.md`:** no
    DML ever (`INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` — a worksheet function mutating cells
    outside its own return value is the exact anti-pattern Excel's calc engine
    exists to prevent); window functions out of this hydration entirely,
    demand-driven only; `EXPLAIN` (the parsed logical plan returned instead of
    executed) and the persistent index cache stay at the ceiling — and per
    `DATALOG`'s own recalc-cache conclusion above, the index cache is
    profile-first on a real workbook, never speculative.

- ⬜ **`PROLOG(knowledgebase, query)`** — the existing toy (`_1_is_2.`,
  `_Is_1_2?`, `QUESTION`/`STATEMENT` in `scripts/spreadsheet.lisp`) grown from
  sentence-string pattern matching into real unification and backtracking over
  structured facts/rules. **Free-form English-to-query translation is
  explicitly out of scope for this item** — not a technical deferral, the
  owner's own call, this session: Frazaro's whole premise is that one
  deterministic phrasing keeps translation cheap, so if a natural- language
  front end is ever wanted here it is a phrasebook problem (new `{slot:type}`
  grammar rows targeting `(fact ...)`/`(rule ...)` forms, F.4-checked like
  every other rule), never a free-parse problem, and shares no design risk
  with the engine below. **The unifier is substrate, not engine-private
  (scoped 2026-08-29):** v1's substitution-environment unifier is built as
  `VLA_Unify.bas` — shared, DSL-ignorant, `VLA_Relation.bas`'s sibling — not
  inside `VLA_Prolog.bas`, because it has a second client on the day it
  exists: G-RENDER's shipped `UnifyForm` (`VLA_English.bas`, the
  `FormSubstitute` inverse) is already a *one-way* unifier — variables on the
  template side only, a bare `{name}` binds a whole subform, literal atoms
  text-for-text, lists length-for-length — i.e. exactly a unifier's three
  generic cases with one side ground. `VLA_Unify` exposes both modes from one
  walker: one-way match (G-RENDER's case, ground on the concrete side, a
  `Dictionary` of bindings out) and two-way unify (Prolog proper, variables on
  both sides, with the occurs check *decided* rather than defaulted — most
  Prologs skip it for speed; this one refuses by name, `prolog-occurs-check`,
  since a cyclic term can never render, spill, or be audited). `UnifyForm`
  then becomes a thin client for its generic cases. **Corrected at PROLOG.1's
  own build time, not merely scoped:** the glued-slot branch
  (`make-{d}`/`xl{d}`) turned out to need no atom-level hook back into
  `VLA_English` at all — it is pure prefix/suffix string arithmetic over its
  own two arguments, as DSL-ignorant as the other three cases, so `UnifyForm`
  shrank to a one-line call into `VLA_Unify.UnifyOneWay` rather than keeping a
  partial reimplementation. (The original wording here named `mPatItems` as
  what the glued-slot branch reads; that was wrong, found by reading
  `UnifyForm` in full rather than trusted — `mPatItems` belongs to a
  different, later gate, `VLA_English.bas`'s own `CandidateShapeOk`, which
  re-checks a render candidate's typed slots AFTER `UnifyForm` has already
  succeeded, entirely outside this walk.) Three things get simpler at once:
  G-RENDER's own deferred v2 (multi-statement templates — matching a list of
  forms against a list of templates is the unifier's list case, already),
  OPTIMIZE (its grounding step is unification against ground facts: one-way
  mode), and SD-16's wall — because the one thing the unifier is never handed
  is a token stream; it matches forms against forms, and a sentence is not a
  form until `TryPhrase` has already accepted it. *Pays into:* G-RENDER v2,
  OPTIMIZE, AS.4. **Not reopening the `DATALOG` boundary:** an earlier session
  considered and rejected letting `PROLOG()` auto-detect a function-free
  ruleset and silently run it bottom-up instead of backtracking — a query that
  loses its termination guarantee the moment one rule happens to use a
  compound term, with no signal to the author, is the opposite of this
  project's own auditability-before-procedural-power instinct
  (`BETA_REARVIEW.md`'s own words for it). `DATALOG` stays its own
  guaranteed-terminating engine; `PROLOG` stays general and non-terminating by
  design; nothing below revisits that split. **Signature decided now, owner
  call, 2026-08-31, ahead of any real UDF surface existing (SQL.1's own
  precedent — a real signature can be pinned before the item that first
  exposes it is built):** `=PROLOG(clauses, ParamArray tables())`. `clauses`
  (not `programText`, not the title's own original `knowledgebase, query`
  order) because it is the real Prolog term of art — a program IS a set of
  clauses, facts are unit clauses, rules are clauses with a body — and it
  matches this family's own naming pattern of naming a param after what
  dominates the blob (`SQL`'s `queryText`, `DATALOG`'s `rulesText`); the query
  itself is expected to arrive as an embedded `(query ...)` goal inside
  `clauses`, `DATALOG`'s own exact shape, not a second top-level parameter —
  `DATALOG(rulesText, ParamArray tables())` has no separate query argument
  either, and `PROLOG`'s own facts/rules are S-expression text the same way,
  unlike `SQL`'s named-argument Ranges. `tables` is the `ParamArray`, last by
  the same hard VBA rule `SQL`/`DATALOG` already both rely on, reserved for
  PROLOG.6's own live-table-sourced facts (referenced by predicate name from
  within `clauses`, exactly `DATALOG`'s own convention) — not "multiple
  knowledgebases," which this shape has no use for. Hydrated below into
  PROLOG.1–PROLOG.6 plus a stated ceiling — SQL's own flat numbered shape
  (each item builds machinery a later item consumes, never the reverse), not
  `DATALOG`'s MVP-plus-stretch nesting, chosen because this chain is genuinely
  linear start to finish (a two-way unifier before anything exists that can
  unify a rule head against a subgoal; ground facts and queries before rules
  exist to call; rules and backtracking before cut/arithmetic/negation have a
  search to prune) with no independent stretch spokes the way `DATALOG`'s
  negation and aggregation were. `BETA_REARVIEW.md`'s own v0/v1/v2/Ceiling
  breakdown predates this numbering and is superseded by it below; its
  Ceiling-tier ideas (first-argument clause indexing, tabling/SLG, an
  `EXPLAIN` proof tree) are carried forward unhydrated as this entry's own
  stated ceiling, deliberately left unnumbered rather than promoted into a
  PROLOG.7, since nothing built so far demands them.
  - ✅ **PROLOG.1 — `VLA_Unify.bas`, one-way match mode; `UnifyForm` becomes a

    (`VLA_English.bas`, read in full before scoping this) into new module

    glued slot (`make-{d}`/`xl{d}`/`format-as-{d}`, prefix/suffix stripping)
    binds what's between, a literal atom matches text-for-text, a list
    recurses element-by-element at equal length — `bn`/`bv` Collections out
    (this codebase's own ad-hoc-record convention, unchanged),
    `VLA_Relation.bas`'s sibling per this entry's own already-decided design.
    `UnifyForm` shrank to a literal one-line call into `VLA_Unify.UnifyOneWay`
    — **corrected from this bullet's own original wording while building it:**
    every case, including the glued-slot branch, turned out fully DSL-ignorant

    atom-level hook back into `VLA_English` was needed at all; the top
    paragraph's own earlier `mPatItems` reference was wrong too, corrected
    there in the same pass (see that correction for the real gate `mPatItems`
    actually belongs to). No parser, no facts, no rules yet — the smallest
    slice that proves `VLA_Unify`'s own substrate-sharing claim against a
    REAL, already-shipped second client (G-RENDER) before anything
    backtracking-shaped gets built on top of it. **A real gap, found by

    FIXED rather than merely flagged:** the original never checked
    repeated-variable consistency — a template repeating the same `{name}`
    slot let each occurrence bind independently, with `RenderBoundLookup`
    silently returning whichever occurrence it scanned first.
    `VLA_Unify.UnifyOneWay` now enforces consistency (`UnifyBind`,
    `FormsEqual`) — checked against the loaded corpus, not assumed:
    `english_expanded.vla`'s own `paste-values` rule repeats `{r}` twice

    concrete call with two DIFFERENT ranges could have silently matched this

    assumption: a binding must be APPLIED to later comparisons, not just

    still the only mode `UnifyForm` calls) threads a substitution environment
    through the walk. **One real design fork resolved by reading code, not
    assumed, and it went the other way from the obvious first guess:** the
    environment is `envN`/`envT`, two parallel Collections generalizing
    PROLOG.1's own `bn`/`bv` — NOT `VLA_Runtime.VlaDictNew()`, even though
    `VLA_Datalog.bas`'s own module header describes SD-8's identifier fold as
    "correct for a predicate/variable name" (which would argue for the
    case-insensitive `VlaDictNew`, whose `CompareMode` is `vbTextCompare` by
    construction). Grepped `VLA_Datalog.bas` for every `VLA_Identity.Fold`
    call site to check that claim before trusting it: every single one folds a
    PREDICATE-shaped name (`fact`/`rule`/`query` keywords, predicate names) —
    none folds a variable's own text. The header's prose overstated its own
    code. Two Prolog variables differing only in case past their first letter
    (`Foo` vs `FOo`) are genuinely different variables, not one identifier
    spelled two ways, so this module stays case-sensitive throughout (VBA's
    own default), matching what `DATALOG` actually does rather than what its
    header claims it does. Also uses a DIFFERENT variable convention than
    PROLOG.1's own `{name}` bracket syntax — English-template-specific, never
    present in a real program term — adopting instead the classical
    Prolog/Datalog convention (`DATALOG`'s own `IsVariableAtom`, repeated
    locally as `IsVarAtom` rather than cross-module-coupled for a two-line
    rule). Every variable-to-term binding is occurs-checked before being added
    (`EnvOccurs`, walking the fully-dereferenced term) — refused by name
    (`prolog-occurs-check`, now registered in `VLA_Messages.bas`) rather than
    skipped for speed, this project's own already-decided divergence from most
    real Prolog implementations, since a cyclic term could never later render,
    spill to a worksheet, or be audited. **Confirmed, not assumed:** two-way
    unification is not one-way match "run twice" — one-way's ground-side case
    never needs substitution application at all, so `UnifyTwoWay` is new code
    end to end, including a `NthInto`-style `EnvWalkInto`
    Sub-with-`ByRef`-`dest` (a bare `x = objectValue` Variant assignment
    invokes the object's own default member instead of copying the reference —
    this codebase's own documented trap, `VLA_Datalog.bas`'s own `NthInto` the
    precedent followed here). Tested standalone against hand-built form
    literals — no fact/rule text parser needed, since the unifier "is never
    handed a token stream; it matches forms against forms" — proving the
    algorithm before PROLOG.3 gives it real program text to run on. Files:
    `src/VLA_Unify.bas`
    (`UnifyTwoWay`/`EnvWalkInto`/`EnvOccurs`/`EnvBind`/`IsVarAtom`),
    `src/VLA_Messages.bas` (`prolog-occurs-check`, new). Tests:
    `src/VLA_Tests_Query.bas`, `TestUnifyTwoWay`, dispatched from `TestDSLs`
    (ground-constant match/mismatch, a variable binding to a constant and to a

    literal-atom case already has a comment naming three lines above it in the

    evaluated even when `aw` held a Collection (a compound term), invoking the

    call site in `VLA_Unify.bas` was audited against this same class of bug
    after the fact and found already correctly guarded by a separate,
    enclosing `IsObject` statement.

    via its own `Tokenize`/`ParseAll`, nothing DSL-specific, so a real
    interpretation layer is still needed on top of it. `(fact (predicate

    variables; a query is the only place a variable may appear at this stage.

    tom (color red)))` is an ordinary, accepted term, recursively), since
    compound-term nesting is exactly what makes Prolog's unification a
    superset of Datalog's flat positional matching. **Two real corrections
    made while building this, not merely scoped, both catching this bullet's
    own earlier wording:** *(1)* a conjunctive query does NOT reuse PROLOG.1's
    one-way mode as originally scoped — that mode's variable syntax is

    convention PROLOG.2 already built for. `UnifyTwoWay` is what actually gets
    called (correctly, since it degenerates cleanly to one-way behavior
    whenever one side is fully ground, which every stored fact always is),
    reusing PROLOG.2's own substrate directly rather than PROLOG.1's, the
    reuse this bullet's own earlier text got backwards. *(2)* No
    `ParseAtom`-style atom-record abstraction was needed at all, found by

    flat record specifically because it forbids compound terms and needs cheap

    already-generic unifier, does not carry that constraint, so its own
    parsing layer ended up genuinely smaller than `DATALOG`'s. **A real

  - ✅ **PROLOG.4 — `(rule head body...)` forms, unification-driven SLD
    resolution with backtracking, no cut.** `~weeks` — the largest single item
    in this line. Reuses PROLOG.2's two-way unifier as its own resolution
    step: proving a subgoal against a candidate clause head unifies the
    subgoal's own (possibly partially-bound) arguments against the clause
    head's own, both potentially carrying variables — the exact case
    PROLOG.1's one-way mode cannot serve. New machinery this item alone needs,
    not reducible to any prior item: clause-variable RENAMING ("freshening")
    on every invocation, so the same rule text used twice in one proof
    (directly, or through recursion) never lets two invocations' own variables
    collide — standard Prolog practice with no precedent yet in this codebase
    (`DATALOG`'s own facts/rules are read once and fixed for the whole

    backtracking, not native recursion-with-yield — VBA has no
    continuations/generators to suspend a search and resume it later, so "try
    the next clause" is state this item builds on a stack, not a language
    feature it borrows. A hard resolution-step budget, refusing by name past
    the ceiling — this entry's own top paragraph and `SQL`'s own top paragraph
    both already freeze this requirement under SD-4: unlike every prior item
    in this file, `PROLOG` has no termination guarantee by design, and an

    interpreter-loop-only), so this is the item where that named refusal
    actually gets built, not merely promised. All solutions collected into the

    including the two below - plus a full round of hand-verified in-cell

    backtracking, nested compound-term matching, an acyclic graph reachability
    query, nullary predicates composing with ordinary ones in one rule body, a
    reporting-hierarchy tie-back to DATALOG's own motivating example, and
    every named parse-time refusal) and committed.** **One design point this
    bullet stated as settled, reopened and corrected at build time, not
    silently overridden - the same discipline PROLOG.1/PROLOG.3 already
    applied to earlier scoping mistakes in this same file:** this bullet's own
    text above calls for "a real, explicit choice-point stack for
    backtracking, not native recursion... VBA has no continuations/generators
    to suspend a search and resume it later." Reasoned through explicitly
    rather than trusted, because SD-4's own frozen output contract changes the
    premise: `PROLOG()` always returns the WHOLE solution set in one spilled
    array, eagerly - never one solution at a time on demand the way an

    once a rule's body can invoke the same or another rule recursively, depth

    non-terminating by design. `PROLOG_MAX_STEPS` (`VLA_Prolog.bas`, a new

    by name (`prolog-step-ceiling`) past the ceiling; it is set conservatively
    low FOR A SECOND REASON beyond the business-logic one, checked and
    reasoned about rather than assumed: this recursion's own native VBA call
    depth grows one frame per resolution step along the currently-explored
    proof path (unlike `DATALOG`'s flat round loop), so a worded refusal must
    fire before VBA's own raw "Out of stack space" ever could -

    to REAL exhaustion (not skipped the way `SQL.7`/`DATALOG`'s own
    round-ceiling tests are, since one PROLOG step is far cheaper than one

    (`is`/arithmetic) is purely additive, a new body-item KIND with no

    other three. **Reserved words, decided once for all four rather than one
    at a time:** `is`/`not`/`findall`/`!` may never be used as a predicate
    NAME in a `(fact ...)`/`(rule ...)` definition, checked and refused from

    now means a knowledge base written against 5.1 alone can never be silently
    broken once 5.2-5.4 ship, SD-4's own "a shipped spelling keeps its
    meaning" applied to predicate names rather than to program syntax. **One
    design point corrected at 5.1's own build time, not left standing:** this
    bullet's own text above called for cut to reuse "PROLOG.4's own recursive
    backtracking search directly" via "a signal threaded back up through it" -
    still the right shape for 5.4 when it's built, but the mechanism is now
    confirmed rather than assumed: `SolveGoalList`'s own recursive call stack
    already IS the choice-point structure (no separate data structure needed),

    below this depth" signal through it, not building new search machinery.

    - ✅ **PROLOG.5.2 — negation-as-failure (`not`).** Owner-tested live
      (`TestDSLs` 302/302, plus nine live `=PROLOG(...)` cell-formula checks
      spanning ground negation both ways, negation as a filter over an
      already-bound variable, negation inside a rule body over a fresh
      existential variable, the phantom-column non-leak, the shared
      step-ceiling, the error-propagates-out-of-`not` case, and the
      malformed-shape refusal) and committed. `DATALOG.1`'s stratified
      negation is the nearest sibling in spirit (both refuse a case that can't
      be soundly enumerated) but not in mechanism, and this divergence is
      real, not an oversight: `DATALOG` proves stratifiability at PARSE time
      and keeps its termination guarantee; `PROLOG`'s own negation-as-failure
      has no such proof available (a non-terminating sub-goal negated is
      simply non-terminating), so it inherits PROLOG.4's own RUNTIME
      step-budget refusal instead of a parse-time check. Needs a genuinely new
      microscope: a bounded sub-call that runs `SolveGoalList` in isolation (a
      cloned env, discarded regardless of outcome) just to check whether at
      least one solution exists, inverting success/failure - built once here,
      reused directly by PROLOG.5.3's own `findall`. **Built as
      `SolveNegation` (`VLA_Prolog.bas`):** clones `envN`/`envT` via
      `VLA_Unify.UnifyEnvClone`, runs `SolveGoalList` on the negated goal
      alone with an empty `freeVarNames`, discards the clone regardless of
      outcome, and shares `stepsTaken` (ByRef) with the caller rather than a
      fresh sub-budget, so a non-terminating negated goal hits the identical
      `prolog-step-ceiling` refusal ordinary recursion already does.
      Deliberately has no `On Error` of its own: negation-as-failure catches
      proof FAILURE only, never a raised error (a divide-by-zero or
      unbound-variable `is` inside a negated goal propagates all the way out,
      confirmed live-tested). **One real design fork, hand-traced rather than
      assumed:** a variable appearing ONLY inside a negated goal's own
      argument must never become a free query-output column (unlike `is`'s own
      target Var, which genuinely binds in the shared, non-discarded outer
      env) - `CollectVars` now recognizes `(not Goal)` and skips descending
      into `Goal` entirely, confirmed against `(query (not (foo X)))`
      collapsing to a boolean scalar rather than spilling a phantom one-column
      "X". `ValidateBodyItem` gained a `(not Goal)` case (arity exactly 2,
      `prolog-not-bad-shape` otherwise) that recurses into itself to validate
      `Goal` - nested negation and `not` composing with `is` both fall out for

  - ✅ **PROLOG.7 — comparison operators (`<`, `>`, `=<`, `>=`, `=:=`, `=\=`)
    as goals, not folded into `(is ...)`.** SHIPPED 2026-09-08 —
    `VLA_Prolog.bas` (`ComparisonOpFor`, `SolveComparison`, new arms in
    `SolveGoalList`/`ValidateBodyItem`/`DesugarBodyItem`),
    `VLA_Messages.bas`, `VLA_Tests_Query.bas`
    (`TestPrologComparison`, 43 new proofs) and a new ratchet,
    `tools/check_prolog_form_attribution.ps1`. Owner-verified live: all
    fifteen in-cell steps passed, `TestDSLs` 335 → **378/378**, and the
    three untouched baselines held exactly (pure 1047/1047, host 143/143,
    VerifyReports emitter and interpreter 141/141 each) — the byte-identical
    `(is ...)` rendering below is why they did not move. Two claims in this entry's
    own original text were **wrong**, found by reading the code before
    building and recorded here rather than silently corrected:
    - It said each side is evaluated "the way `(is ...)`'s own right-hand
      side already is (`ComputeArithmetic`, recursively)". Wrong entry
      point. `(is ...)`'s RHS is evaluated by **`EvalArithTerm`** — the
      recursive walker that dereferences through the env and refuses an
      unbound or non-numeric leaf by name; it delegates only its innermost
      binary op to `VLA_Relation.ComputeArithmetic`, which never walks an
      env. `EvalArithTerm` is what a comparison calls, once per side.
    - It said `prolog-arith-unbound-variable`/`prolog-arith-not-numeric`
      "fire identically" — true, and precisely the problem it did not
      name: their TEXT was hard-coded to say `(is ...)`, so a user who
      wrote `(> Salary 80000)` would be told about a form they never
      wrote. That is the same confidently-wrong-answer defect `IN.15`
      closed. **The entry counted two such messages; there are five** —
      it missed `prolog-arith-divide-by-zero` and both parse-time
      refusals (`prolog-arith-unknown-operator`, `prolog-arith-wrong-arity`),
      which a comparison reaches as soon as its operands are validated the
      way `(is ...)`'s already are. A sixth text,
      `prolog-reserved-predicate-name`, enumerated "is/not/findall/!" and
      would have become quietly wrong about what it had just refused.
      The undercount was caught by writing
