# THE CLOSED LEDGER — items moved off the roadmap

*Since 2026-09-27, `BETA_ROADMAP.md` holds only open work. An item that becomes ✅ (owner-tested and committed) is moved here the day it closes, verbatim, under the department and section it was filed in; its full build record is the matching entry earlier in this file, and "(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)" points at it. New closures are appended at the end of this section, so the line numbers above stay where every citation left them. First sweep, 2026-09-27: 91 items moved, nothing edited but the pointers.*

## 🛡 ADVERSARY · SECURITY

- ✅ **SEC.0 — the threat model, written down.** `docs/THREAT_MODEL.md`, owner-reviewed: what a program may reach, what a phrasebook may reach, who is trusted at each layer — and the finding that "zero-trust runtime" (IN.9's phrase) means "no Trust Center prompt," not "every capability verified." Written against the real dispatch code, not the roadmap's description of it. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)*

- ✅ **SEC.1 — capability gating of dynamic dispatch (Tier 0 + Tier 2 only).** Built and owner-verified live (`VLA_SELF-TESTS` pure 947/947, host 143/143; `VerifyReports` emitter 141/141, interpreter 141/141) and committed. The `CallByName` fallback in `DynamicGet`/`DynamicCall`/`DynamicSet` is removed from shipped builds; a 25-member census (not just G-TABLES — plain cell-`.value` reads and cross-sheet `.range` lookups too) was promoted to native `Select Case` arms first, closed by subtraction second. Tier 1 (permissioned/declared capabilities like `vlasendmail`) is scoped separately as `SEC.7`, not part of this item's own completion. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)*

- ✅ **SEC.2 — `raw` behind explicit, per-phrasebook consent.** Gated at `EnglishLoadVocabulary` (the file loader), not the shared host-free `EnglishLoadVocabularyText` — the correction a purity-ratchet check forced. Two chained dialogs; two remembered scopes (this workbook via a document property, this device via the registry), keyed by `EnglishSourceHash` so any edit re-prompts; no test-bypass toggle anywhere. Owner-verified live. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)*

- ✅ **SEC.4 — formula/CSV-injection guard.** A program-written cell *value* beginning with `=`/`+`/`-`/`@` is neutralized with a leading apostrophe (`NeutralizeFormulaInjection`, the `Value` sink only). Owner-tested live, including the formula-bar check. Deliberately not applied to formula writes, which are a feature. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)*

- ✅ **SEC.5 — `SECURITY.md` and a disclosure contact.** Owner-reviewed and committed (`docs/SECURITY.md`) — contact address (`english@spreadsheet.company`) and response commitment (3-business-day acknowledgment, no fixed remediation deadline, severity-prioritized, reporter kept informed) both filled in by the owner rather than guessed. A place a finder is told to report to, and a stated response commitment — the minimum credible artifact before any external pilot (`PI.*`) or public download. *Honest tension, named rather than solved here:* `SD-13`'s no-network stance means a disclosed vulnerability has no push-update path to the people already running an affected build; this item does not resolve that, it only makes sure a report has somewhere to land. `~hours`

- ✅ **SEC.8 — programs in cells bypass Office's macro policy (Mark-of-the-Web unread).** The architectural one. Built and owner-verified live 2026-09-08 (eight live tests, all passed; `VLA_SELF-TESTS` pure 1011/1011, host 143/143; `VerifyReports` emitter 141/141, interpreter 141/141; `.xlam` builds and compiles clean). **The question that could have killed the item was answered first and holds: Excel does NOT strip the Mark-of-the-Web on "Enable Editing"** - the refusal fired on a marked workbook after the banner was cleared, which is the only state that matters. A plain `.xlsx` carries its program in cells; after "Enable Editing" the interpreter ran it with the add-in's privilege, reaching `Workbooks.Open`/`SaveAs`/`SaveCopyAs`, PDF export, print, sheet-protect and an Outlook draft natively — no `Zone.Identifier`/Protected-View check anywhere in `src/` (re-grepped at build time). *Built:* `VLA_Provenance.bas` reads the host workbook's `Zone.Identifier` alternate stream (VLA_Loader's own ADODB idiom), `VLA_IDE.CaptureHost` captures the zone once per command (D1's chokepoint), and **nine** dispatch sites refuse per-site, naming the verb — six egress (`Open`/`SaveAs`/`SaveCopyAs`/`ExportAsFixedFormat`/`PrintOut`/`VlaSendMail`) plus three destructive-to-local-data (`Close SaveChanges:=`/`Protect`/`Unprotect`), a deliberate widening past the four this tranche first listed. **No trust store, deliberately:** granting is Windows' own out-of-band Unblock, so there is nothing for a hostile workbook to pre-fill — which is why SEC.8 does **not** depend on SEC.10/SEC.11. **Positive-signal-only, and that is forced:** an absent mark and an unreadable one (non-NTFS) fail with the *same* error (`0x800A0BBA`), so fail-closed would refuse every ordinary local file; an unreadable mark is trusted only on a demonstrably local path, and refuses on UNC/`http(s)://` (known false-positive class: a workbook opened straight from a SharePoint URL; OneDrive-*synced* folders are ordinary `C:\` paths and unaffected). **The memo, not `ActiveWorkbook`, is what the guards read** — `activate` is itself dispatchable, so a per-site `ActiveWorkbook` read would let a marked workbook launder its provenance through an innocent one. *Pinned by* `VlaSelfTest`'s `TestSec8Provenance` (the whole decision: parse, path class, policy, guard refusal — no COM) and `tools/check_sec8_provenance_gate.ps1` (every site guarded *inside its own `Case`*, and `CaptureHost` still captures; mutation-tested red and green on four mutations; it found a tenth site on first run, exempted with its reason). *Coverage gap, stated as SEC.13 stated its own:* the pure suite cannot fabricate a Mark-of-the-Web, so nothing automated proves a real marked workbook is refused — live-test only; and the gated list is human judgement a baseline scan cannot discover for itself. **Open empirical question that decides the item:** whether Excel strips the mark on "Enable Editing" — if it does, the gate is inert and only `ReadZoneStream`'s *source* changes, not the design. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~days`–`~weeks`

- ✅ **SEC.9 — phrasebook search-order hijack + silent replay of workbook-stored paths.** `IdeVocabPath` preferred `<workbook dir>\scripts\english.vla` over the add-in's own copy (DLL-hijack with a `.vla`), and GO.6's `VLA_LoadedPhrasebooks` document property replayed absolute/UNC paths with no prompt (UNC also leaks NTLM on Check). Ship a workbook with a grammar file beside it and every sentence means what the attacker says. **The one item in the tranche whose mechanism was OBSERVED LIVE** (2026-09-08, benignly: a stale `english.vla` in Downloads loaded ahead of the add-in's own copy, and failed loudly only by luck — it was too old to know `put`). **Built and owner-verified live 2026-09-08 (nine live tests across four passes, all passing; pure 1047/1047, host 143/143; `VerifyReports` 141/141 and 141/141; both `.xlam` build clean).** *Built:* one gate, `PhrasebookPathApproved`, on the only two loaders that derive a path from something the **workbook** controls; the decision is recorded **device-side** keyed by **(path, digest)** — the workbook property is the *request*, the registry is the *answer*, and only the answer is trusted (so this does not repeat SEC.10's mistake of storing the permission slip inside the artifact it authorizes). **The order of operations is the security property:** in the replay loop the gate runs *before* `SafeFileExists`, because `Dir$` on a UNC path leaks this machine's credentials before returning; a path with no recorded decision is never touched at all. The host-directory candidate is **kept and demoted**, not deleted — a decline falls through to the built-in grammar rather than refusing — and declining is **recorded and skipped quietly** rather than raised, because nothing can remove an entry from `VLA_LoadedPhrasebooks` and a loud refusal would trap the user. *Pinned by* `TestSec9PhrasebookPaths` (19 pure assertions on the two string predicates, prefix trap and OneDrive `https://` host path included), `TestSec9DeniedPhrasebookIsNotReplayed` (the gate actually gates, proven positively through the real loader), and the new **`tools/check_sec9_phrasebook_gate.ps1`** — which pins that **approval precedes probe**, mutation-tested red on all five mutations. **The security mechanism was right on the first pass; everything AROUND the refusal was not, and that is the item's real lesson** — four live passes each found a defect in *remembering* a decision (an empty digest could never match itself, so a "no" re-asked forever), *showing* it (the first visibility fix landed only in `VlaDiagnostics`, which lives in `VLA_DevRig.bas` and never ships — it is now in the shipped *Copy Diagnostic Report*), and *undoing* it (the claimed escape hatch, Load Phrasebook, ADDS a phrasebook onto the base while a sibling override REPLACES it, so it could never re-approve the case that needed it). Resolved with a 23rd ribbon button, **Forget Phrasebook Approvals**, chosen by the owner over session-scoped denials: a permanent content-keyed "no" avoids the dialog habituation that a prompt reappearing every session would train. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~days`

- ✅ **SEC.11 — the consent hash is a 32-bit polynomial.** `EnglishSourceHash` was `h*31+b mod 2³²` over non-whitespace bytes; second preimages are trivial (edit two comment bytes), so even device-scope consent transferred to a crafted phrasebook. **Built and owner-verified live 2026-09-08 (nine live tests, all passed; pure 1024/1024, host 143/143; `VerifyReports` 141/141 and 141/141; both `.xlam` build clean)**. The consent modal fired for a `raw`-bearing phrasebook, stayed silent after a whitespace-only edit, and **returned** after a one-character token edit. **The twins were then checked on real data:** VBA and PowerShell independently produce the identical 64-hex digest and identical 89,446 byte count for `english.vla`, and the legacy reader reproduces `F972F88B` — the value actually stamped in the artifact since `0.5.1`. **The minted fix did not survive contact:** `CreateObject("System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256Managed")` **FAILS on the owner's own machine**, both bitnesses, `0x80131700` — the ProgID resolves through `mscoree.dll` to *mscorlib 2.0*, and only .NET v4 is installed. That is the Windows 11 default (Framework 3.5 is an optional feature, off), so shipping it would have made every `raw`-bearing phrasebook unloadable here. CAPICOM is unregistered too; a `bcrypt` P/Invoke would spend `SUBSTRATE.md` H.4's one-`Declare` census. *Built instead:* `VLA_Digest.bas`, **SHA-256 in ~150 lines of pure VBA** — no COM, no `Declare`, no fallback to test, and pure, so `VlaSelfTest` covers it completely against FIPS 180-4. **Owner decisions:** hashes the **same whitespace-stripped stream** (`.gitattributes` gives CRLF checkouts, so a raw-byte digest would give one phrasebook two identities on two machines — and skipping whitespace costs nothing, since an attacker was always free to vary the non-whitespace bytes); old grants are **namespaced** (`SEC2RawConsentV2`), not migrated or deleted, since re-prompting is fail-safe and `SEC.10` will move workbook scope anyway; stamps gain an explicit `sha256:` prefix and `check_rule_coverage.ps1` now reads **three** generations while writing only the newest, so **no exported artifact breaks**. *Pinned by* `TestSec11Digest` (published vectors + the 55/56/64/65 padding boundaries) and the new **`tools/check_hash_twin.ps1`**, which lifts the *real* `Get-SourceHash` out of its script and pins both sides to the **same FIPS vectors** — retiring the "change one side and you must change the other" comment that is the exact shape which has bitten this project nine times. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~hours`

- ✅ **SEC.13 — Word automation opens untrusted documents with macros enabled.** Built and owner-verified live 2026-09-08 (`VLA_SELF-TESTS` pure 985/985, host 143/143; `VerifyReports` emitter 141/141, interpreter 141/141) and committed. *Import Program File…* (menu and ribbon, `EnglishIdeImport`) accepts `.docx`/`.doc` — and `ImportFromPath` routes `.docm` **explicitly**, worse than this line first said — through `ReadWordFile`, which never set `AutomationSecurity`, so Word's automation default (*Low*) ran a `.docm`'s AutoOpen silently; `GetObject` also attaches to the user's live Word. *Fixed:* `ReadWordFile` captures the prior value, sets `3` (`msoAutomationSecurityForceDisable` — the literal, Word being late-bound) **after** `On Error GoTo cleanup` so an unsettable guard refuses instead of opening unguarded, and restores it on both exit paths — only on an *attached* instance, since one we created is quit anyway. Restore is deliberately silent (its failure leaves Word *more* restrictive, never less), so no new message id and the raw-raise ratchet still reads `VLA_IDE` = 1. Asking before opening a document at all stays `SEC.7`/`SEC.8`'s scope, not this one's. *Pinned by* `tools/check_word_automation_security.ps1` (every `Documents.Open` must set the guard earlier in its own procedure; mutation-tested red and green). *Coverage gap:* the pin proves the guard is present, not that it works — three behaviours (macro suppressed on a created instance; on an attached one, with its setting restored; restored on the `cleanup:` error path too) rest on one live test each, all run and passed, none automatable without launching Word. Fixture recipe: `archive/sec13_word_fixture.md`. *Robustness follow-on, ✅ owner-verified live:* `DisplayAlerts = 0` (`wdAlertsNone`, the literal) on an instance Frazaro **created** only, so a modal Word chose to show on an invisible window can no longer appear to hang Excel; deliberately NOT on an attached instance, which is visible and whose alerts are not ours to silence — that direction fails *open*, unlike the `AutomationSecurity` restore. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~hours`

## 🗣🔧 LANGUAGE + MACHINE · THE TWO NEUTRALITIES

### Part A — language-neutrality

**A2 — the catalogues (defer past beta)**

- ✅ **LX.5 — split `VLA_English.bas`** into language-neutral sentence machinery and English-specific rules. *Why it mattered:* it decided whether `VLA_Spanish.bas` is a sibling or a fork — answer: sibling, proven live, not just argued. **Session finding, sharpened by a direct audit:** the structural remainder isn't just the four headline forms — `ParseStmt`/`ParseCond`/`ParseExpr`/`ParsePrim`/the Oxford-comma list logic (5 call sites) compare tokens against dozens of literal English words, and the existing head-table alias system (`VlaHeadTableAliasMap`/`ResolveHeadAlias`) turns out to be no help at all: it only resolves *emitted* VLA s-expression heads inside `VLA.bas`, never English sentence tokens.
  **Phase 1 (committed) — the canonicalization seam:** a new `CanonicalizeStructuralWords` pass (runs right after every `EnTokenize` call that feeds `ParseStmt`) rewrites any bare-word token a phrasebook has aliased via a new `(keyword-alias "si" "if")` directive to its canonical English spelling — same alias-map shape `VlaHeadTableAliasMap` already proved, staged one step earlier, so every existing comparison site is untouched and English behavior is provably unchanged (empty alias table = no-op). Oxford-comma-list grammar's own positional rule stays universal, fixed core syntax, per LX.1's own "keep, structural" ruling — only its trigger words go through the table.
  **Phase 2 (committed) — the physical split:** a direct variable-usage audit of all 216 procedures against the file's ~65 shared `Private` Collections found the split was NOT the "~2/3 neutral" first estimate — `mPatItems` alone was touched directly from 13 different regions spanning the whole file, so grammar registration, the DCG matcher, G-RENDER, statement/condition/expression parsing, vocabulary loading, and the front door itself (`EnglishToVla` drives the parse loop directly) are one connected, inseparable unit. **204 of 216 procedures moved** to a new `VLA_SentenceEngine.bas`; `VLA_English.bas` keeps only the twelve pure, stateless functions LX.1's audit already called "data" (`NumberWord`/`OrdinalWord`/`ExprOpWord`/`IsExprOpWord`/`IsNoiseWord`/`IsDroppedWord`/`SkipArticles`/`IsColorWord`/`SlotDesc`/`StrayCharHint`) plus Phase 1's own keyword-alias mechanism. Every moved procedure kept its exact name and visibility — VBA resolves an unqualified `Public` call project-wide regardless of which module hosts it, so no caller anywhere in the project needed to change. `VLA_Build.bas`/`VLA_DevRig.bas` manifests, `VLA_Tests_Host.bas`'s stray-helper scan, and the `check_raise_ratchet.ps1`/`check_translate_purity.ps1` module-name ratchets all updated and re-verified clean against the new file.
  **Phase 3 (committed) — the second-language proof:** `scripts/polyglotta/espanol.vla` gets five `(keyword-alias ...)` entries (si/es/repetir/veces/mientras) and three `test-success` proofs exercising real Spanish `if`/`repeat`/`while` sentences — the first non-English sentences in this project to reach `ParseStmt`'s own structural dispatch, not just the DCG phrase matcher. `TestLx10NonEnglishFixture` (`VLA_Tests_Grammar.bas`) validated these for free: `EnglishLoadVocabulary` raises on any `test-success` mismatch at load time, so the existing fixture running clean *was* the proof, not a weaker proxy for it — no new test needed. **Confirmed live:** `VlaSelfTests()` 903/903 pure + 119/119 host, `VlaGoldens()` diff empty, `TestLx10NonEnglishFixture` itself PASS. **`for each` deliberately excluded, found not guessed — the one real remainder:** `en`/`para` are already ordinary vocabulary elsewhere in `espanol.vla` ("... en la celda", "envia un correo PARA ..."), and `CanonicalizeStructuralWords` rewrites every occurrence of an aliased word globally, not just in structural position — aliasing either would break existing rules in the same file. Real fix (named, not built): canonicalize only when the *preceding* token already resolved to a structural word expecting a second one, not on every token unconditionally — a future item, now with a real, found reason rather than a hypothetical one. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)*

### Part B — target-neutrality: the interpreter as the runtime

**B2 — the evaluator (weeks; the runtime, so no longer contingent)**

- ✅ **IN.15 — sixteen `VLA_Runtime` helpers refused with a VBE crash dialog instead of a Frazaro modal.** Not a security item: a correctness and UX bug hitting every user, no attacker involved. `Application.Run` does not propagate a target macro's `Err.Raise` to the caller's handler (proven standalone, `archive/VLA_Diag2.bas` scenario 1), so any helper whose job includes *saying no* could not say no — a bad colour in a sentence produced "Run-time error '5'" with a **Debug** button, in direct violation of `LX.8`'s refuse-in-words doctrine. Fixed with a native `Case` per helper in `TryRuntimeHelper`, which puts the raise back on the ordinary VBA stack. **The count was scoped by hand as eight and is actually sixteen** — the other eight raise only through the shared private `RequirePivotTableByName` (`rt-pivot-not-found`, a misspelled pivot table name) and are invisible to a scan that reads each helper's body alone. The new `tools/check_runtime_raise_dispatch.ps1` computes that transitively and found them; written first, mutation-tested both directions, it is the reason the number is right, and that is this item's main lesson. Also replaces `TryRuntimeHelper`'s `If Err.Number <> 0 Then handled = False` — one line that conflated "is this a real helper?" with "did the helper refuse?", and could have reported a deliberate refusal as `interp-head-unresolved` — with a `VlaHelperManifest` membership test made *before* the call, soft-failing to "fall back", never to "nothing is a helper". *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~days`

**B3 — a second host, prepared (SD-18's own infrastructure; target-neutrality applied one substrate further than IN.\* ever needed to)**

- ✅ **PORT.1 — pure, host-free translate entry points.** `VLA_Browser.bas` (named for the client, not the network — nothing about it implies an SD-13-violating connection): `EnglishTranslateTextToVla`/`ToVba` take phrasebook text in memory, never touch a file, never show a dialog. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)*

- ✅ **PORT.2 — the translate-path purity ratchet.** `tools/check_translate_purity.ps1`: scans a named set of (module, function) pairs for forbidden host touches — body-only by design, so a callee is verified by reading, not by the exit code. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)*

- ✅ **PORT.3 — the intrinsics spec.** `docs/INTRINSICS.md`: the VBA-specific string/array/comparison behaviors a non-VBA port must match, each earned by a real citation. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)*
- *Together:* SD-18's infrastructure — a port with no purity guarantee and no intrinsics reference would re-litigate every behavior. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)*

The shipped `Format cell … as currency` is that bare `$`: it has always meant the machine's currency (a CO.7 candidate). *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~days`

It also fails a slot of 32 bits or fewer in the 64-bit branch that its reviewed list does not name (eleven today, all frmCLI's), two branches of one name out of step, a name some host has no Declare for, and a Declare in generated text (a VBA string literal, `.vla`, `.vba`). Not user-visible, but RELEASES.md carries it under 0.6.0 as a release check. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~hours`

## 🪟 PRODUCT · PERFORMANCE

- ✅ **PF.4 — array slabs for range reads/writes.** Two orders of magnitude on row loops, owner-verified live (2026-09-04). Deliberately *not* the invisible, pattern-detected rewrite this bullet first promised: the owner flagged the determinism/auditability risk and `docs/CONSULTANT.md`'s own doctrine ("every emitted line is derivable by hand from visible source") confirmed it, so the fast path is visible in the source rather than silently inferred. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)*
**PF.4a — array-element `set!`/read parity, ✅ owner-verified live (2026-09-03).** A real gap found during scoping, both directions: `(set! (arr i) v)` and `(arr i)` already worked compiled via plain text substitution (`EmitStmt`/`EmitExpr`'s own generic `Case Else`), but the interpreter had neither - `ExecSet` raised `interp-set-place-not-object`, `EvalDynamicHead` raised `interp-head-unresolved` - nothing in the existing corpus ever needed either direction before. Fixed as two purely-additive fallback tiers. **A real bug caught by the owner's own first live run, not reasoned through in advance:** both tiers' first draft called `VLA_Runtime.VlaDictGet` directly to test "is this bound to an array" - but `VlaDictGet` is deliberately loud on a miss (`rt-dict-key-missing`), not a safe try-get, so a plain `(range "a1")` place (also `Count = 2`) raised "there is nothing stored at key 'range'" for every ordinary bare-place Range assignment - 10 host failures, all `TestStmtParity`/one IN.2 case, never the pure suite. Fixed by guarding both tiers with `VlaDictHas` first, the existing non-raising check already built for exactly this shape. `VlaSelfTestsAll`: 910/910 pure, 125/125 host, clean on the second run.
**PF.4b — bulk read/write-back runtime helpers, owner-verified live (2026-09-04).** `VLA_Runtime.VlaSlabRead`/`VlaSlabWrite` - **a real design correction caught before landing, not after:** the first plan was delegating to `VLA_Relation.SourceToArray`'s already-correct bulk-read pattern, until re-reading `VLA_Runtime.bas`'s own EN_RUNTIME INJECT BOUNDARY (the exact text copied verbatim into a standalone user workbook, with NO other add-in module available there - the same V5.3 problem this module was split out to solve originally) showed that would raise "Sub or Function not defined" the moment the add-in isn't present - exactly IN.9's own "export" scenario PF.4's performance claim is actually about, not just interactive add-in use. Built self-contained instead (R7's own precedent - this module's `Fold` already duplicates rather than depends, for the identical reason). Neither function is ListObject-aware or strips a header row (a SQL/DATALOG-specific convention, not a general one); `.Value` throughout, not `.Value2`, to behave exactly like the `Cells(i, j).Value` loop it replaces. Tests: `TestArraySlabHelpers` (multi-row/col with a real mutate-then-verify, 1x1, 1-row/N-col, N-row/1-col).
**PF.4c — the `for-each-row` form itself, owner-verified live (2026-09-04).** `(for-each-row (row range) body...)`, wired to `PF.4a`/`PF.4b`. Bulk-read the range once into `arr`; `row` is not a real emitted variable at all - `(row i)`/`(set! (row i) v)` compile DIRECTLY to `arr(iVar, i)` (a dynamic-extent substitution in `EmitExpr`, checked ahead of its normal dispatch, save/restored around the body the same way `mAtLine`/`mGenRow` already are). One bulk write-back after the loop. All-or-nothing commit falls out of that shape with nothing special-cased: `VlaSlabWrite` is the one commit point, called once, after the loop, and because nothing is ever deferred into a separate buffer, a bare `exit-for` needs no cooperation of its own - whatever's mutated up to and including the break's own row is already sitting in `arr` the moment it fires. `return` does not commit (`EmitReturn`'s bare `Exit Sub`/`Exit Function` always leaves the whole procedure) - the interpreter's own `ExecForEachRow` checks `mProcReturn`/`mGotoLabel` first to match, a real cross-backend asymmetry caught during scoping. "a raised error discards everything" - argued from the shape, then owner-confirmed live (2026-09-03): a genuine out-of-bounds error mid-loop (rows 1-2 already mutated in memory, row 3 raising before ever reaching it) left the range fully unchanged after both Run and Interpret, on a real workbook. Body is in-place read/modify/write only for now - no raw `Cells`/`Range` calls inside it. Tests: `TestStmtParity` gains a full round-trip case and a break-commits-partial case. **Three real bugs caught live across two owner-run passes, not reasoned through in advance:** (1) a hidden bookkeeping name, `cVar`, collided with `CVar` - a real VBA intrinsic (Convert-to-Variant) - turning `Dim cVar As String`, alone on its own line, into a bare "Syntax error." (2) the string-building was reshaped from one long continuation into separate `r = r & ...` appends, matching `EmitFor`/`EmitForEach`/`EmitIf`/`EmitSelect`'s own style. (3) the real design flaw, found by `VlaSelfTestsAll`'s own break-commits test: the original fix for (1)/(2) still sliced each row into its own small array, ran the body, then copied it back into `arr` in a SEPARATE loop placed AFTER the body - so `exit-for` skipped that trailing copy-back, losing the mutation on the exact row where the break fired (`20 + 20 + 30 = 70` measured live, not the expected `90`). Fixed by removing the separate row array entirely for the direct-substitution design above, deleting the copy-back step - and the whole bug class - rather than special-casing `exit-for` to route through it correctly. `~weeks`

- ✅ **PF.7 — `VlaEmbeddedText`'s own O(n²) string-build.** Every embedded-sheet load (Check/Compile's vocabulary and prelude, `IdeLoadVocab`'s chain) concatenated cell by cell through COM; replaced with one bulk `.Value` read and a `Join`. Found during P-TOK's what's-next pass; owner-verified live. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)*

Now on `DATALOG.16`'s exact map, and `VLA_Relation.bas` no longer calls `VLA_Runtime`. Pinned by `TestSqlGroupCase`; live, a Table holding `Bob`, `bob` and `Bob` spilled `Bob 2 11` / `bob 1 5` (one row, `Bob 3 16`, before). A named limit stays, at `AggSignature`: an aggregate's signature carries a string literal as written and is still a `VlaDict` key, so `MAX('Bob')` beside `MAX('bob')` would share one slot — contrived now, ordinary once `SQL.10`'s `CASE WHEN` lands, so close it there. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~hours`

Owner-flagged: PROLOG.5.1 shipped arithmetic strictly as a *binding* form, so there was no `(> Salary 80000)` to write — the README's own staffing example had to route around it. New dispatch in `SolveGoalList`, sibling to `not`/`findall`/`!`: a comparison goal succeeds or fails, it never binds, and it sits above the `clauseDict` lookup because an unknown predicate there is a silent dead end. Each side is evaluated by **`EvalArithTerm`** (this entry originally named `ComputeArithmetic` — wrong; that is only the leaf substrate `EvalArithTerm` delegates to), then compared by `VLA_Relation.CompareValues` with `bothNumeric:=True`. The five shared arithmetic refusals hard-coded `(is ...)` into their own text — the entry counted two, a check written first found five — so they are now `{form}`-templated, byte-identical when rendered for `(is ...)`, and pinned by `tools/check_prolog_form_attribution.ps1`. **DATALOG.6 inherits that shape** for its own `sum`-specific text. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)*

There was no way to unify two terms as a goal mid-body, only implicitly at head-matching time. New dispatch in `SolveGoalList` sibling to `is`/`not`/`findall`/comparison, above the `clauseDict` lookup for the same silent-dead-end reason. This entry was stale three ways — it called the chain three arms reserving FOUR names; `PROLOG.7` had already made it four predName-keyed arms and TEN reserved names, which `tools/check_prolog_reserved_names.ps1`, written first, printed on its first run (third consecutive item whose hand count was wrong). **The proposed `\=`-as-`(not (= X Y))` desugaring was rejected**: it would make the refusal name a form the user never wrote, the exact defect `PROLOG.7` just removed, and would spend a whole `SolveIsolated` sub-proof on one `UnifyTwoWay`. **The binding fork the entry omitted**: `UnifyTwoWay` leaves a failed walk's bindings behind, so `=` and `\=` both clone — `=` threads its clone forward, `\=` discards it, `==`/`\==` never bind. **A phantom-column bug it did not anticipate**: `(query (\== X Y))` succeeds, so `CollectVars` needed a skip over the three non-binding operators, with `=` excepted — `UnificationBindsOutward` is `"unify"` alone, since `\=` runs the binding primitive but keeps nothing. `==` needed a NEW `VLA_Unify.TermsIdentical` (dereferences at every node; the existing `FormsEqual` answers False to `(= X 1) (== X 1)`), transliterated and run against 22 cases before import. **Occurs check decided**: `(\= X (f X))` inherits `=`'s refusal; `==`/`\==` never reach a bind and answer ordinarily. **The live pass turned up a sharp edge, not a defect**: `TableCellToTerm` stores a text cell as `Chr$(34) & value`, so a bare `eng` in a query is a different atom from the `"eng` in the fact — `(\= D eng)` matched every row and `(== D eng)` none, both correctly. `PROLOG.6`'s deliberate convention (it stops a cell reading `Alice` being read as a variable), now pinned by two pure tests and called out in `RELEASES.md`; whether a bare symbol *should* match a text cell is now its own decision item, `PROLOG.10`, and is not taken here. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)*

X)` before landing, because in an S-EXPRESSION language `(atom bob)` is visually identical to a compound DATA term — `(color red)`, `(f a)` — where real Prolog's grammar separates goal from term by position and ours does not. Decisive evidence found by grep, not argument: **`VLA.bas`'s macro layer already reserves `car`/`cdr`/`cons`/`list` beside `null?`/`eq?`/`equal?`**, and the three with `?` are exactly the three that ask a question — so the convention was already house style, unstated, and the bare spelling was the *inconsistent* one. Rule now stated: an alphabetic goal that asks about one term ends in `?`; one that produces a value does not — hence `between` keeps none. Reader unchanged (`?` is not a `Tokenize` delimiter). **The cost, paid not dodged:** `(atom X)` would have been an unknown predicate and so a SILENT dead end, the exact class this item's tests were designed around — so the six bare ISO names are **reserved AND dispatched to a refusal naming the `?` form**, `IN.15`/`PROLOG.7`'s move. Aliasing both spellings was rejected. Reserved set **27 names**, twelve from this family: six that solve, six that teach. **They are TWO shapes, and the entry's one bullet hid it:** the six type tests are deterministic and bind nothing (`not`'s shape), while `between/3` is a **GENERATOR — the first in this dispatch** — recursing once per *value* like the candidates loop, which is why `SolveBetween` alone takes `rest`/`solutions`/the cut signal. This entry was stale three ways; the substantive one repeats `PROLOG.8`'s undercount shape: "a cheap shape check over `IsVarAtom`/`TermHasVariable`'s existing classification" is **false** — `IsVarAtom` answers `var`/`nonvar` and nothing else, `TermHasVariable` answers a different question none of the six asks, and **`atom`/`number` needed numeric classification the entry never names**, which is exactly the half that collides with `PROLOG.10`. **That collision is answered LOCALLY and explicitly not closed:** the marker is identity-bearing, so `(atom? "42")` TRUE and `(number? "42")` FALSE, coherent with `PROLOG.8`'s shipped `"42 \== 42`; written down once in `LeafIsNumberTerm`, which `between` also asks. A transliteration over 25 term shapes × 6 predicates **before import** measured that `PROLOG.10`'s option B would move **exactly two** cases. New datum for `PROLOG.10`: `EvalArithTerm` already strips the marker, so arithmetic says "same" while identity says "different" — the engine answers its open sub-question both ways today. `between` **refuses** a non-whole or non-numeric X rather than failing (keeping test mode and generate mode the same relation), **fails** on an empty range, and is bounded by `PROLOG_MAX_STEPS` with **no private budget** plus an up-front range refusal so a wide range is not misdiagnosed as a runaway rule — usable range is therefore **119**, an engine limit stated rather than hidden, and `PROLOG_MAX_STEPS` was deliberately **not** raised. What changes is that COMPARING them stops being silent, because `(\= D eng)` succeeding on every row of a table is a confidently wrong answer. **Scoped on four objective criteria, not taste:** (i) `(\= D eng)` returning every row is WRONG, while a plain `(query (emp N eng))` returning zero rows is RIGHT-but-unhelpful, and this project's doctrine is about wrong answers; (ii) MONOTONICITY — raising during clause matching would let a NON-matching clause abort a query that has a real match, and adding a fact must never remove a solution; (iii) PRECEDENT — `PROLOG.9` ruled the same way three times one item earlier; (iv) REVERSIBILITY — the scoped reading is a strict subset and can be widened later, the unscoped one could only be narrowed by retracting an error class. **Two entry claims failed:** "no false positives" missed the false positive on a *successful query*, and the entry blamed shipped-test flipping on option B alone when **D flips `(= "eng" eng)` too** — necessarily, since that pin IS the confusable case; re-pointed, not retired. **The diagnosis cannot mis-blame:** a two-way "is there a marker-only pair anywhere" test would blame the marker for `(= (f "eng") (g eng))`, whose real difference is `f` vs `g`, so the classifier answers three ways and fires only on marker-only; transliterated over 16 shapes before import, which surfaced an undocumented speculative-`outText` contract. Open sub-question answered in the wording: a TEXT 42 and a NUMERIC 42 are still different terms, and the refusal calls the bare side a "number", not a "name". **Left open deliberately:** the plain query still returns zero rows silently — correct-but-unhelpful, so below the bar; the deferred mechanism can add it later without changing semantics. Minted 2026-09-18 out of `DATALOG.12`'s four live passes, the owner's call; the cause is measured and the fix is settled. A `DATALOG` answer costs about 1.4 ms per source row plus 0.14 ms per further column, flat, so 1,000 rows takes 2.25s and 10,000 stalls Excel for 25.5s. No algorithm degrades with size, and returning cells to Excel is free. The cost is one line, three times: `VlaDictGet`, `VlaDictHas` and `VlaDictSet` each open with `TypeName(d) = "Dictionary"`, and `TypeName` on a late-bound COM object costs 0.148 ms — as much as creating the dictionary — while asking it of a VBA `Collection` costs nothing. A row makes about a dozen such calls, which is 85% of it; reading the code had predicted `CreateObject` per tuple, which is 12%. Three ways to stop asking were weighed, and the owner settled it 2026-09-18 on measured numbers: **`TypeOf d Is Collection`** — stateless, one line per wrapper, and it makes the `Collection` fallback the tested branch rather than the dictionary. Both cheap options measured 0.000 ms against `TypeName`'s 0.145, so the price is asking COM a question at all, not which one; the typed `VlaDict` class was the permanent answer and the largest diff (102 call sites in `VLA_Datalog.bas` alone), and was not taken. The same guard also stands in `VlaDictKeys` and `VlaDictPairs`, and twice in `VLA_Relation`'s membership index — grepped 2026-09-18, not timed, and a scoping question for the build. Bounded honestly: about threefold, not a cure — 100,000 rows stays out of reach. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~hours`

## 🪟 PRODUCT · INTERFACE

- ✅ **CLI.3 — the console remembers: session history.** Continues `IN.13`'s own sub-pass numbering (`CLI.0`–`CLI.2` live in code comments). Every command text the console runs — refused ones included, so they can be fixed — goes into a capped, duplicate-collapsed buffer in a standard module (the form unloads on Esc, so it cannot hold it). Recall on Ctrl+Up/Ctrl+Down, never bare Up/Down, which move the caret inside a multi-line `defmacro`; a half-typed text is kept as entry zero. A `history` word prints the last N, numbered, and `!N` recalls one. Code only: the form's `.frx` layout is untouched. Unblocks SPITBALLS 25. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~hours`

- ✅ **CLI.4 — history survives Excel.** `CLI.3`'s buffer persisted to a text file in the user's profile (`%APPDATA%\Frazaro\`), multi-line entries escaped or length-prefixed; read as data, never executed; a read failure is silent, a write failure is a status-line note. Not the workbook (a mailed workbook would carry your transcript — `SEC.10`'s lesson, milder) and not the registry (`SaveSetting` is for short values). The first use of the profile folder in the product, and the precedent SPITBALLS 27's `init.vla` needs. *Depends on:* `CLI.3`. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~hours`

- ✅ **CLI.5 — the transcript pane, and the last three results.** A read-only pane under the input showing each command and what came back — the status, `debug-print` output, refusals, and an expression's value — which means `VlaCliRun` returns the value beside its status. The only slice that changes layout, so `tools/build_cli_form.ps1` regenerates the `.frx` (owner-run: it drives Excel over COM) and `UserForm_Resize` learns a second band. The last three values are `*`, `**` and `***` - checked at building: the reader reads them as ordinary atoms, `*` in head position is still multiplication, and `(last)` would have claimed the word for good while it already means "the last element of". The window the owner settled on over five live looks: Run and Clear History (Ctrl+Shift+Del) along the top, the box, and the transcript along the bottom; no status line, hint line or Close button, Esc closing from anywhere, and nothing that needs the mouse. Unblocks SPITBALLS 15, 47, 50 and 101. *Depends on:* `CLI.3`. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~days`

- ✅ **U.19 — a failed Undo snapshot must not leave its copy behind.** **Built, owner-verified live and committed 2026-09-14.** A snapshot now keeps a list of every sheet it makes and removes them all if any step fails. It finds its copy by the name that is new, not by tab position (the old read could rename the wrong sheet without any error). A name the scan finds that no sheet can have, like `'Q1/Q2'!`, is no longer a target (its marker's rename failed on every Run). A failed snapshot now stops the Run before its first sentence with `ide-undo-snapshot-failed`, where it used to carry on without Undo and say nothing. Measured live on the old build: the position lookup was the cause. A copy made after a very-hidden last sheet lands before it, so the rename silently hit the `Output` tombstone. That left `probe19 (2)` visible and a blank snapshot, so Undo would have put the sheet back empty. It happened on every Run that names an existing sheet. Minted 2026-09-13 from `G-PROLOG` slice 1's live pass, where one Run left tabs `gp1` and `gp1 (2)`; filed to scope and build separately. `TakeRunSnapshot` copies a sheet (Excel names it `<sheet> (2)`), then renames and very-hides it; if that raises, the Run swallows the error with only an Immediate-window note, so the copy stays visible, is never rolled back, and the user is not told Undo is gone for that Run (the tombstone branch has the same shape, and Undo's own error text already warns of "a stray copy of a program sheet"). Why the rename failed is unknown: measure first (the Immediate-window text, one Run or two, the very-hidden `VLAu_` sheets). Then roll back on failure and say it in words (`LX.8`). *Pays into:* `U.17`. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~hours`–`~days`

- ✅ **U.20 — Lint VLA must never break a file it rewrites: audit the button.** **Built, owner-verified live and committed 2026-09-14** (compile and `VlaSelfTest` clean; eight live tests, checked on disk by `tools/u20_lint_fixture.ps1 -Check`, 12/12 PASS). Mechanism confirmed from code: `WriteTextFileVlaIde` was ANSI `Print #` (cp1252 writes `£` as the lone `A3` seen), plus one extra trailing CRLF — which every linted `.vla` on disk still carries, so it is kept on purpose. `VLA_Lint.VlaLintFileBytes` (pure, bytes in/out, pinned by `TestU20LintFileBytes`) keeps BOM and LF-only breaks, refuses a `; GENERATED` artifact, invalid UTF-8, and any rewrite that moves a non-whitespace byte (the stamp hash's filter, compared directly) — which catches the formatter's two known meaning changes, a `;` comment inside a form and a lone `\` in a string. Lint VLA writes only via a verified `.lint-tmp` sibling plus a rename; the folder flow plans every file and shows the plan before the first overwrite. Exposure, scanned offline over every tracked `.vla`: no in-form comment, lone backslash, trailing token or BOM anywhere; `english.vla`'s `£` is the only non-ASCII. Export Expanded Phrasebook and Coverage now write UTF-8 too. *Found, not in scope:* `instructions_golden.vla` is generated but unstamped, and `WriteTextFileVla` is still ANSI (filed as TER-5 and TER-6). *Follow-on, owner-verified live and committed 2026-09-14:* `VLA_Build.WriteTextFile` now writes UTF-8 - no BOM for `version.iss` and the ribbon XML, a BOM for the ribbon-injection `.ps1` (Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads a BOM-less script as ANSI); a rebuild left `version.iss` and the XML byte-identical and the `.ps1` identical plus its BOM. *Original entry:* Minted 2026-09-14, the owner's call, after a Lint VLA click during `G-PROLOG` slice 2's live pass rewrote files in `scripts/polyglotta`, the generated `english_expanded.vla` among them. The working `english.vla` came back re-flowed with one character changed: a comment's `£` written as a lone `0xA3` byte, invalid UTF-8, which moved the source hash and made a fresh export read as STALE (the tested text was restored before commit). Likely cause, to verify: `WriteTextFileVlaIde` writes with VBA's ANSI `Open … For Output` + `Print #`, and Export Expanded Phrasebook and the coverage report share it. Audit: a UTF-8, line-ending-preserving, idempotent write pinned by a non-ASCII round trip; formatting that may change whitespace only, refused if the non-whitespace hash would move; generated artifacts refused by name; exposure across every `.vla` first. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~hours`–`~days`

- ✅ **U.21 — Undo finds the copy it restores by name.** Minted 2026-09-14 as a follow-up to `U.19`. **Built, owner-verified live and committed 2026-09-14.** `EnglishIdeUndo` took its restored copy as `hb.Worksheets(snap.Index + 1)`. `Index` counts every sheet but `Worksheets` skips chart sheets, so a chart sheet anywhere before the snapshot made it rename the wrong sheet. A restore that failed part-way also left the person's sheet renamed `VLAu_old` beside a visible stray copy. Now the copy is the one new sheet name (`VlaIdeAddedSheetNames`). A failed restore removes that copy and gives the set-aside sheet its name back. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~hours`

- ✅ **U.22 — program tags compare without case.** Minted 2026-09-14 from `U.19`'s finding (c). **Built, owner-verified live and committed 2026-09-14.** Excel sheet names ignore case, but tags were compared exactly in four places: Add Program's guard, the Run and Undo guard, the snapshot sweep, and Undo's match. So `Frazaro (G-p1)` beside `Frazaro (gp1)` shared every snapshot name. Changing only the capitals in a program's tab stranded its old copies, and since `U.19` every later Run of it was refused. `VlaIdeTagsMatch` now folds case at all four places. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~hours`

- ✅ **U.23 — a refused Run keeps the previous Undo.** Minted 2026-09-14 as a follow-up to `U.19`. **Built, owner-verified live and committed 2026-09-14.** The snapshot deleted the previous Run's copies before making any new one, so a Run that `U.19` refused left Undo with nothing to put back. New copies are now made under a staging prefix (`VLAn_`). They replace the previous ones only once every one exists. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~hours`

A Run that stops part-way (a refusal, or any error no `Try:` catches) now puts back what Undo Last Run would, from the snapshot it took before its first sentence, and only then speaks: one message with the line and sentence (`TER-10`), the stop's own words, the sheets put back and the sheets it had made that are gone again, and that a file saved or an email drafted stays as it is. Both backends: a compiled program's step handler now hands its stop to a new runtime helper, `VlaReportStop`, which records it when the Run button armed it and otherwise shows it as before, without "Excel says" (most stops are Frazaro's own refusals). *Depends on:* `U.19`, `U.23`. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~hours`

## 🪴 TERRARIUM · DEFERRED, NON-CRITICAL BUGS

- ✅ **TER-2 — stale row-error marks survive a Check after the row's content is deleted.** **Built, owner-verified live and committed 2026-09-14** (second live pass: all five tests passed). The marks are in column C, not B; `ClearMarks` now clears to whichever is further, the program's last row or column C's own last mark, so a deleted last sentence (or a whole deleted program) loses its mark on the next Check. The live pass also found that the empty-program guard on Check, Compile, Interpret, Export and Show VBA could never fire ("Subscript out of range" in C1); fixed. A newly created workspace tab now opens with B1 active. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* *As filed:* Owner-found live, 2026-08-27, during L0.2's regression, root cause checked against the code, not just observed: `ClearMarks` (`VLA_IDE.bas`) only clears `B1:B<lastRow>`, and `lastRow` is `IdeLastRow(ws)` recomputed fresh on every call - if the row carrying the failing mark was the sheet's last non-empty row, deleting that row's content shrinks `lastRow` itself, so the clear range no longer reaches the very cell holding the stale mark it needs to erase. Fix direction, not yet built: `ClearMarks` needs to clear against the sheet's prior extent (or a safely-large fixed bound), not the freshly-recomputed one.

- ✅ **TER-5 — generated `.vla` files carried no `; GENERATED` stamp, so Lint VLA would reformat them.** Found by U.20's exposure scan, filed 2026-09-14. `instructions_golden.vla` (`VlaWriteGoldens`) and `instructions.vla` (Translate to VLA) were generated but unstamped. **Built, owner-verified live and committed 2026-09-14** (self-tests 1134/1134 and 152/152, goldens pass, `tools/ter567_fixture.ps1 -Check` 11/11): both writers stamp line 1 deterministically (no date, no folder; the golden's stamp goes on after `VlaTranspile`, so the `.vba` golden is unchanged), and the generated-file refusal now says the first line tells how to make the file again. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)*

ASCII output is byte-identical. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)*

- ✅ **TER-7 — a program with no sentences failed with "Subscript out of range".** Filed 2026-09-14 from TER-2's live pass. `EnTokenize` did `ReDim (1 To 0)` for zero tokens - an empty, whitespace-only or comments-only program - which VBA refuses. **Built, owner-verified live and committed 2026-09-14:** zero tokens give `(0 To 0)`, the empty list every reader already expects; pinned by `TestTer7EmptyProgram`. *Found here, fixed as `TER-8`:* `VLA.bas`'s `Tokenize` had the same `ReDim`, reached by DATALOG and PROLOG with empty rules text. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)*

A proof's one `(tables ...)` clause holds its tables, each written as an answer is: a name, a header list (an Excel Table, whose columns a keyed atom may name) or `headless` (a plain named range), then its rows in the order written, every cell as a live Table's `Value2` gives it (a bare `007` is the number 7, `"007"` the text). The runner reads the clause into what a live Table argument is to every engine, a folded name and a Table-shaped array, and makes DATALOG's table arguments from it afresh for every run; PROLOG's, SQL's and the third gear's proofs will read the same arrays. Twenty-nine pins moved as twenty-six proofs (124 in all), with thirteen controls for the clause: `TestDatalog`, `TestDatalogBuiltins` and `TestDatalogKeyedAtoms` retired whole, and the six keyed refusals that accepted any error name their ids. Both parity loops hand a proof's tables to each engine, so OPTIMIZE and the integer grounder answer those programs; the table fell 99 → 76 and the call-site ceiling 109 → 84. The clingo translation declines a table, so its export stays 23. Found while building, and filed as `DATALOG.17`: a number written in a program is matched against a fractional number cell through `CStr`, which follows the machine's locale. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~days`

## 🗣🔧 LANGUAGE + MACHINE · THE TWO NEUTRALITIES · Part B

- ✅ **IN.17 — the interpreter's built-ins took the arguments they expected and ignored the rest.** Audit C3, confirmed live by the owner 2026-09-28; **built, owner-verified live and committed 2026-09-29** (`VLA_SELF-TESTS` pure 1537/1537 as predicted and host 241/241; `TestDSLs` 2330/0; `VerifyReports` 317/317 on both backends, six rows new; the goldens as predicted; five hand tests, with `inputbox`'s title and default not run live). Under Interpret, `contains` and `starts with` never held and `does not contain` always did: English writes VBA's four-argument `InStr`, and the interpreter's `instr` read two, so it searched the text "1". Every `TryEvalBuiltin` arm now takes exactly the argument counts VBA's own function takes (`instr` 2–4, `round` 1–2, `msgbox` and `inputbox` 1–3, the rest one count) and refuses any other by name (`interp-builtin-arity`); `msgbox` answers the button pressed, so a raw `(msgbox "hi")` in the CLI shows 1. Pinned at each count, and by six GText corpus rows that fail under Interpret if a condition is read wrongly either way. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~hours`

Pinned by four pure checks and a host test that first shows Excel hiding the apostrophe. *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~hours`

The snapshot now comes first and the workspace sheet after, so a sheet the run made carries a removal marker like every other, and the stop's and Undo's existing words say "Removed the sheet the run had created". *(more: the full entry, earlier in this file)* `~hours`

- ✅ **U.29 — a Run gives back Excel's settings as it found them.** Minted 2026-09-30 at `G-FORMULA` slice 3's scoping, as its precursor, from the audit's `C62`: a Run put back only screen updating, so a program that turned calculation off or wrote in the status bar and then stopped left every open workbook in manual calculation, or the words showing, for the rest of the Excel session, where Undo cannot reach. **Built, owner-verified live and committed 2026-09-30** (pure 1567, host 265, `VerifyReports` 349/349 on both backends; three hand tests on both backends). Calculation, the status bar, alerts, events and screen updating are recorded before a Run's first change and given back on every exit of both Run procedures, finished or stopped, each as the run found it, so a person working in manual keeps manual; cut or copy mode left on is cancelled; the program sheet is protected only when it had no protection.
